### Sheet: `Payroll Scope Summary`

| Dimona — PAYROLL SCOPE SUMMARY |  |  |
| --- | --- | --- |
|  |  |  |
| Who and what must be declared through Dimona, and what the payroll engine is responsible for. Dimona is not a pay calculation: it opens and closes the employment relationship in real time and is the key against which the quarterly DmfA is validated (CCG Module 10.1). |  |  |
|  |  |  |
| ITEM / SCENARIO | IN SCOPE? | NOTES / REASONING |
| ═══ WHO GETS DECLARED ═══ |  |  |
| Every employee subject to Belgian social security, whatever the contract length | YES | The obligation attaches to the employment relationship, not to a threshold. A one-day contract is declared. |
| Students under a student contract (worker type STU) | YES | Declared with planned hours, which consume the 650-hour annual quota. The quota consumed must be reconciled against the Student@work counter (SIR IN-05) BEFORE filing, because it selects the solidarity contribution instead of ordinary contributions. |
| Flexi-job workers (worker type FLX) | YES | Declared per quarter. The glossary restricts the declaration to no more than 31 days before the start of the quarter of entry into service. |
| Occasional workers in horeca and agriculture (worker type EXT) | YES | Declared per day with start and end times, and the INSZ becomes mandatory (zone 00024 presence: obligatoire for EXT). |
| Construction workers (worker type BCW, RTA) | YES | Joint committee 124. The C3.2A control card numbers (zones 00663, 00664) become mandatory. |
| Temporary agency workers | YES | The agency files the Dimona and completes the UsingEmployer block (90107) with the user undertaking's name and enterprise number. |
| Posted workers coming into Belgium | NO | Covered by the Limosa declaration (BE-NSSO-005, OUT-08), not by Dimona, where the home social security scheme continues under an A1 (CCG Module 11.2). |
| Self-employed contractors and company directors without an employment contract | NO | No employment relationship, therefore no Dimona. A misclassification exposes the client to the requalification rules. |
| Provincial and local administration personnel (PPL / APL) | NO | Zone 00109 (NUMÉRO PPL) is left at zero. Out of scope for this build; the APL worker-code annex (Annexe 28) is not held. |
| ═══ TIMING AND RELATIONSHIP ═══ |  |  |
| Filed before the employee starts work | YES | CCG Module 1.2 and Module 10.1. A late IN is an offence and, more practically, it blocks the DmfA occupation line for the quarter. |
| End of employment declared by the first working day after | YES | The DimonaOut block quotes the Dimona period identification number returned by the NSSO on the accepted IN. |
| Derived from another filing | NO | Dimona is a separate, event-driven declaration. CCG Module 10.1 filing-mechanics table, control C4. |
| Blocks the DmfA if rejected | YES | The DmfA is validated against the Dimona. This is the single most important operational dependency in the Belgian chain. |
| ═══ AMOUNTS AND CALCULATIONS ═══ |  |  |
| Carries any wage amount | NO | Dimona carries no remuneration whatsoever. Not one field in the 57-zone glossary is an amount. All pay data travels in the DmfA (BE-NSSO-002). |
| Carries planned hours and days | YES | Zones 01135 and 01017, for the worker types where the quota matters — principally students. |
| Requires a wage type mapping to BE-WTC-001 | NO | There is no amount to map. The mapping this declaration needs is of master data — worker type, joint committee, contract type — onto NSSO code lists. |
| ═══ SPECIAL CASES ═══ |  |  |
| Daily registration for EXT and STU (block 90480) | YES | A separate declaration per day worked, quoting the Dimona period identification number of the covering period. |
| Correction of an accepted Dimona | YES | Through DimonaUpdate (90378) quoting the period identification number, or DimonaCancel (90379) where the relationship never began. |
| Worker types A17, QUA, STX, TEA | NO | Closed by the NSSO. The glossary records that A17 and QUA can no longer be declared (from 2022/1 and 1 January 2023 respectively), STX since 2014/1, and TEA is obsolete from 2022/1. The engine must reject them at entry rather than let the channel reject the file. |

### Sheet: `File Structure`

| Dimona — FILE STRUCTURE AND TECHNICAL SPECIFICATIONS |
| --- |
|  |
| ═══ FILE FORMAT ═══ |
| Format            XML (structured message), validated against the NSSO Dimona XSD in the TechLib. |
| Alternative       REST v2, POST /dimona/v2/declarations, Content-Type application/json. |
| Alternative       Secured online service, Dimona Mobile app, or the unsecured web form (one declaration at a time). |
| Encoding          NOT FOUND - requires direct inquiry to the NSSO. Governed by the application XSD; see BE-SIR-001 gap G1. |
| Transport         SFTP or FTP on the social security extranet, application code DIMN. |
|  |
| ═══ BATCH FILE NAMING — NSSO SFTP MANUAL v14 SECTION 8 ═══ |
| Declaration file  FI.DIMN.<sender>.<YYYYMMDD>.<seq>.<env> |
| Signature file    FS.DIMN.<sender>.<YYYYMMDD>.<seq>.<env> |
| Trigger file      GO.DIMN.<sender>.<YYYYMMDD>.<seq>.<env>   (empty; starts processing) |
| Cancel file       TD.DIMN.<sender>.<YYYYMMDD>.<seq>.<env>   (empty; cancels processing) |
|  |
| FI   the declaration file            FS   the electronic signature file |
| GO   the empty file that starts processing |
| TD   the empty file that cancels processing |
| DIMN the application code for a Dimona declaration |
| <sender>  the sender number allotted when the first channel was created for the quality |
| <YYYYMMDD> the file creation date |
| <seq>     a sequence number, unique per creation date and per environment; any alphanumeric |
| <env>     R = production, T = circuit test (folder INTEST) |
|  |
| The seventh and eighth name parts (total parts and part number) are used for DmfA but |
| NOT for Dimona: the manual states DRS and temporary unemployment declarations cannot be |
| split. A Dimona file therefore has six name parts. |
| The signature file is mandatory in production and optional in the simulation environment; |
| the GO file is mandatory in both. |
|  |
| ═══ XML STRUCTURE — FUNCTIONAL BLOCK HIERARCHY ═══ |
| <Form>                              90059  envelope: identification, creation date and hour, status, type |
| <Reference>                       90082  reference type, origin, number |
| <EmployerId>                      90256  NSSO number, provisional NSSO number, PPL number, enterprise number |
| <NaturalPerson>                   90017  the worker: INSZ, name, birth data, address, nationality |
| <Address>                       90022  generic address block |
| <Dimona>                          90372  container |
| <DimonaIn>                      90373  start date and hour, end date and hour, planned hours, planned days |
| <DimonaFeatures>              90374  joint committee, worker type, sub-entity |
| <SmallStatutesInformation>    90594  employment nature, activity vs risk, worker status |
| <ConstructionControlCards>    90375  C3.2A card numbers — joint committee 124 only |
| <StudentPlaceOfWork>          90376  place of work — student worker type only |
| <UsingEmployer>               90107  user undertaking — temporary agency work only |
| <DimonaOut>                     90377  Dimona period id, end date, INSZ |
| <DimonaUpdate>                  90378  Dimona period id, revised dates and hours |
| <DimonaCancel>                  90379  Dimona period id, INSZ |
| <DailyRegistrationDeclaration>    90480  daily registration for EXT and STU |
|  |
| Exactly one of DimonaIn, DimonaOut, DimonaUpdate or DimonaCancel is present per declaration. |
|  |
| ═══ RESPONSE LEG ═══ |
| The accepted declaration returns the Dimona period identification number (zone 00913). |
| This is registered separately as IN-01 in BE-SIR-001 Section 1 and must be stored against |
| the employment record: every later OUT, UPDATE or CANCEL quotes it, and there is no way |
| to close an employment relationship without it. |

### Sheet: `Population Rules`

| Rule Category | Field Name | Source System | Population Logic | Edge Cases |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ═══ MANDATORY FIELD RULES ═══ |  |  |  |  |
| Identification | Social Security Identification Number (00024) | Employee master data | Populate with the 11-digit INSZ from the national register, or the BIS number where the worker is not registered in Belgium. The number is mandatory for a Dimona IN concerning an occasional worker (type EXT) and optional otherwise, but the engine must treat it as mandatory in all cases: the DmfA keys the worker block on the INSZ, so a Dimona accepted without one will produce a worker who cannot be declared quarterly. Validate the check digits before sending — positions 10-11 must equal 97 minus the remainder of the first nine digits divided by 97, and for a person born from 2000 onwards a leading 2 is prefixed to the nine digits before the division. | Prohibited inside the UsingEmployer block (90107) — the glossary records presence 'Interdit' there. A worker with no INSZ and no BIS number cannot be declared; the BIS number must be requested first. Anomaly 00024-003 (invalid) and 00024-347 (incompatible with the Dimona period identification number) are both blocking. |
| Identification | NSSO Employer Registration Number (00011) and Enterprise Number (00014) | Employer master data | Exactly one identification route must be satisfied. Zone 00011 is mandatory where the employer holds a definitive NSSO number AND zone 00014 is absent. Where the unique enterprise number is known, the glossary permits zone 00011 to be set to zero. The value 0 is never permitted for zone 00011 in a Dimona declaration, so a client without a definitive NSSO number must be declared on the provisional number (00948) instead. Set the values from the client master record, never from the previous declaration. | A client migrating from a provisional to a definitive NSSO number mid-quarter changes identification route between two declarations for the same worker; both remain valid, but the reconciliation against the DmfA must key on the enterprise number rather than on the NSSO number. |
| Declaration type | Exactly one of DimonaIn / DimonaOut / DimonaUpdate / DimonaCancel | Payroll event engine | The four declaration blocks are mutually exclusive within one declaration. Select the block from the employment event: entry into service produces DimonaIn; end of employment produces DimonaOut; a change of a declared date or hour on an accepted period produces DimonaUpdate; a relationship that never began produces DimonaCancel. Never emit a DimonaOut for a contract that was cancelled — that is the Cancel case, and an Out on a cancelled period will be rejected. | A worker whose start date moves forward before the original start date has passed is an Update, not a Cancel plus a new In. Issuing Cancel plus In allocates a NEW Dimona period identification number, which orphans any daily registration already filed against the old one. |
| ═══ CRITICAL VALIDATION RULES ═══ |  |  |  |  |
| Sequencing | Dimona Period Id (00913) | SIR IN-01 — Dimona acknowledgement | This number is never generated by payroll. It is allocated by the NSSO on an accepted Dimona IN and returned on the acknowledgement leg, which BE-SIR-001 registers as IN-01. Store it against the employment record on receipt. Every subsequent Out, Update, Cancel and daily registration for that employment period quotes it, and the declaration cannot be filed without it. It is a 12-digit composite in which the last two positions are a check number over the first ten, so it must be stored and transmitted whole and never re-keyed or reformatted. | If the acknowledgement is lost after a successful send, the period identification number must be recovered by consultation rather than by re-declaring: a second Dimona IN for the same worker and period creates a duplicate period. BE-SIR-001 gap G5 records that the NSSO has not published whether POST /declarations is idempotent, so the engine must not rely on the channel to suppress the duplicate. |
| Timing | Starting Date (00910) | Contract master data | The start date must be declared before the worker actually starts work (CCG Modules 1.2 and 10.1). The glossary bounds the value: it must be earlier than the current year plus ten years and on or after 1920-01-01. Two worker types carry a tighter rule — for a flexi-job worker (FLX) the declaration cannot be made more than 31 days before the start of the quarter of entry into service, and for an Article 17 worker (A17) the glossary states the entry date is constrained, although A17 can no longer be declared at all from quarter 2022/1. | A back-dated start is accepted by the channel but is a late declaration in law. The engine should raise it as an exception rather than file it silently, because the client, not Mercans, carries the offence. A start date in a closed quarter also affects the DmfA occupation line, which must then be corrected through OUT-03. |
| Sector conditional | C3.2A card numbers (00663, 00664) | Sector master data — joint committee 124 | Both zones carry presence 'Indispensable' inside the ConstructionControlCards block, which means the block cannot exist without them; the block itself is only present for construction. Populate zone 00663 with the C3.2A card number for the month in which the Dimona period starts and zone 00664 with the card number for the following month. Both are 12-digit composites. They interact with zone 00046: the block is only valid where the joint committee is 124. | A Dimona period starting on the last day of a month needs both cards, and the second is often not yet issued. The engine must hold the declaration rather than pad the field. |
| Quota | Planned Hours Nbr (01135) | Time and attendance, reconciled against SIR IN-05 | For a student (worker type STU) the planned hours declared here consume the 650-hour annual quota. Before filing, query the Student@work counter (SIR IN-05) for hours already consumed by this student across ALL employers, not only this client. Where the declaration would take the student over 650 hours, the solidarity contribution ceases to apply and ordinary employee and employer contributions become due from the first hour of the excess, which changes the DmfA worker code and the net pay. | The quota is per student per calendar year and is consumed in declaration order across employers, so a competing employer's later declaration can retroactively push this client's hours over the line. BE-SIR-001 gap G18 records that the NSSO has not published whether a batch or web-service channel exists for the quota consultation at all — a web-only check is a real operational constraint on a high-volume student employer, and the engine must not assume an API. |
| ═══ PAYROLL-SPECIFIC POPULATION RULES ═══ |  |  |  |  |
| Master data mapping | Worker Type (00655) | Contract master data | This single three-character code selects the entire contribution and reporting regime downstream, so it is the most consequential mapping in the declaration. Map the Mercans contract type onto the NSSO list in the Field Options sheet. Four values are closed and must be rejected at data entry rather than at the channel: A17 (from quarter 2022/1), QUA (from 1 January 2023), STX (from quarter 2014/1) and TEA (obsolete from quarter 1/2022). Where the contract does not match any open value, use OTH and raise an exception for review — do not guess. | A worker who changes type mid-employment — a student who becomes an ordinary employee on graduation — needs the old period closed with a DimonaOut and a new period opened with a DimonaIn. An Update cannot change the worker type. |
| Master data mapping | Joint Committee Number (00046) | Contract master data | Populate with the joint committee, sub-committee or sub-sub-committee number in the structure the glossary prescribes: CCC left-aligned, or CCC.CC, or CCC.CC.CC. Where the worker falls under no joint committee the glossary provides a specific treatment. This field must carry the same value that will appear on the DmfA occupation line, because a change of joint committee opens a new occupation line in the quarterly declaration (CCG Module 10.1). | Joint committee 124 (construction) additionally triggers the ConstructionControlCards block, and a wrong committee number therefore produces either a spurious mandatory block or a missing one. The register of joint committees is not held in 00-official-sources and is marked NOT FOUND in the Field Options sheet. |
| Master data mapping | Employment Nature (01231) | Contract master data | EMPLOYEE for white-collar staff (bedienden), including a person in civic service; WORKER for blue-collar staff (arbeiders). This is not cosmetic: the blue-collar / white-collar split drives the holiday pay regime, the 108% social security contribution base for blue-collar workers, the DmfA worker code and the departure holiday pay treatment. It must agree with the classification used throughout BE-WTC-001. | A worker whose function changes from blue-collar to white-collar within an employment relationship must have the Dimona period closed and reopened, because the nature is fixed for the period. |
| ═══ CROSS-FIELD VALIDATIONS ═══ |  |  |  |  |
| Cross-field | 00024 INSZ vs 00913 Dimona Period Id | Both | The glossary publishes anomaly 00024-347, 'incompatible with the Dimona period identification number', as blocking. The INSZ quoted on an Out, Update or Cancel must be the INSZ of the worker for whom the period was opened. The engine must therefore take both values from the same stored employment record and never from two different sources. | A worker whose INSZ is corrected after the IN was accepted — a BIS number replaced by a definitive national register number — will fail this validation on the Out. The INSZ change must itself be declared first. |
| Cross-field | 00025-00035 identity block vs 00024 INSZ | Employee master data | The identity zones (name, first name, date of birth, birthplace, sex, address, nationality) carry presence 'Obligatoire si' conditioned on the identification number: they become mandatory when the INSZ is absent or cannot be verified, and are otherwise optional because the NSSO reads them from the national register. Populate them in all cases anyway — the cost is nil and it removes an entire class of rejection for workers whose national register entry is incomplete. | Zones 00168 and 00169 (municipality and country of birth) carry a doubled condition in the glossary ('Obligatoire si si le numéro d'identification...') and are only required in the no-INSZ case. |
| Cross-field | 00046 Joint Committee vs UsingEmployer block (90107) | Assignment master data | Zones 00131 and 00153 (the user undertaking's enterprise number and name) carry presence 'Obligatoire si' conditioned on zone 00046. In temporary agency work the agency is the employer and files the Dimona; the user undertaking is identified in block 90107. Zones 01185 (VAT number) and 01254 (number of successive daily contracts) are recorded as 'Interdit' in a Dimona and must be left empty. | A prohibited zone that is populated is a blocking rejection, not a warning. The engine must suppress 01185 and 01254 for Dimona even though the same block carries them in other declaration families. |

### Sheet: `Payroll Scope Summary`

| DmfA — PAYROLL SCOPE SUMMARY |  |  |
| --- | --- | --- |
|  |  |  |
| Who and what enters the quarterly declaration. The DmfA is one consolidated grid, not a set of separate filings: it carries in a single quarterly submission the wages and working time of every employee, the ordinary and every special contribution, every reduction, and the sectoral fund contributions (CCG Module 10.1). The general rule throughout is that NO NETTING IS PERMITTED — a contribution and its reduction are declared separately, and a gross and its deduction are declared separately. |  |  |
|  |  |  |
| ITEM / SCENARIO | IN SCOPE? | NOTES / REASONING |
| ═══ WHO GETS REPORTED ═══ |  |  |
| Every employee with an occupation in the quarter | YES | One worker block per employee per quarter, keyed on the INSZ, with at least one occupation line beneath it. |
| An employee who left mid-quarter | YES | The occupation line carries an end date (zone 00045). Departure holiday pay is declared under remuneration code 3 (CCG Module 10.1). |
| An employee absent all quarter — long-term sickness, thematic leave | YES | The occupation line persists and the absence is declared through the service codes; zero remuneration is not zero declaration. |
| Students | YES | Through the dedicated student contribution block (90003), with the solidarity contribution, until the 650-hour quota is exceeded. |
| Company vehicles | YES | One CompanyVehicle block (90294) per vehicle, driving the CO2 solidarity contribution per month of availability (CCG Module 10.1). |
| Contributions with no natural person attached | YES | Block 90002 carries employer-level contributions that attach to no individual worker. |
| Public sector and provincial/local administration personnel | NO | Blocks 90411, 90412, 90413, 90172 and 90005 are coloured red and left unpopulated. The APL worker-code table (NSSO Annexe 28) is not held, so this build cannot support them. |
| Self-employed contractors and directors without a contract of employment | NO | Not subject to employee social security; no worker block. |
| Posted workers remaining under a foreign scheme with an A1 | NO | Contributions are due in the home state. Limosa (BE-NSSO-005) applies instead. |
| ═══ TIMING AND RELATIONSHIP ═══ |  |  |
| One consolidated grid covering all contributions | YES | CCG Module 10.1, control C4: there is no separate return per contribution type. Special social security contribution, CO2 solidarity, 8.86% on supplementary pensions, Wijninckx and CBA no. 90 all travel inside this one declaration. |
| Validated against the Dimona | YES | A rejected Dimona blocks the quarterly declaration. This is the single most important operational dependency in the Belgian chain. |
| Generates the 281.10 annual certificate | NO | CCG Module 10.1 is explicit: Belcotax is an independent filing built from the payroll ledger, not derived from the DmfA and not derived from the twelve monthly withholding tax returns. It must be reconciled against them, which is a different obligation from being generated by them. |
| Carries the wage withholding tax | NO | The withholding tax return is filed separately, with a different authority, on a different cycle (BE-FIN-001, OUT-04). |
| Corrected in place | NO | A correction is a separate modification declaration allocated to the ORIGINAL quarter (BE-NSSO-003, OUT-03). |
| ═══ AMOUNTS AND CALCULATIONS ═══ |  |  |
| Amounts expressed in eurocent with no decimal separator | YES | Every amount zone in the glossary is numeric with an implied two-decimal scale. A decimal point in the file is a blocking anomaly. |
| Contribution base and contribution amount declared separately | YES | Zones 00084 and 00085. CCG Module 10.1: per contribution type, the base and the amount separately, never a net figure. |
| Reduction declared separately from the contribution it reduces | YES | Blocks 90109 and 90110. The reduction amount AND the parameters that justified it must both be producible. |
| Blue-collar gross declared at 108% | YES | CCG Module 10.1 lists 'gross at 108% for blue-collar workers' as a required intermediate for the DmfA contribution base. |
| Negative amounts permitted | YES | Amount zones accept a negative value, which is how a within-quarter regularisation is expressed. A correction to a CLOSED quarter is not a negative in the current quarter — it is a modification declaration for the original quarter. |
| ═══ SPECIAL CASES ═══ |  |  |
| A new occupation line when a determining characteristic changes mid-quarter | YES | CCG Module 10.1: a new line whenever the worker code, joint committee, working-time regime, contract type or start/end date changes. The engine must be able to split a quarter on any of these axes. |
| Declarations of up to 49 employees through the online service | YES | The NSSO brochure of 17/10/2024 limits the online service to 49 employees; above that the batch channel is the only route. |
| Splitting a large declaration into parts | YES | The SFTP manual allows a DmfA to be split into a maximum of 9 parts, named with the total-parts and part-number suffixes. DRS and temporary unemployment declarations cannot be split; DmfA can. |
| Monthly advance payments | YES | Where the K-2 threshold of EUR 6,197.34 is exceeded, advances are due by the 5th day following each month of the quarter. The advance amounts are calculated by the NSSO, not by the employer, and arrive on SIR IN-04. |

### Sheet: `File Structure`

| DmfA — FILE STRUCTURE AND TECHNICAL SPECIFICATIONS |
| --- |
|  |
| ═══ FILE FORMAT ═══ |
| Format            XML, validated against the NSSO DmfA XSD published in the TechLib. |
| Encoding          NOT FOUND - requires direct inquiry to the NSSO. BE-SIR-001 gap G1. |
| Transport         SFTP or FTP on the social security extranet, application code DMFA. |
| Alternative       DmfA online service — limited to declarations concerning up to 49 employees |
| (ONSS-RSZ brochure, 17 October 2024). |
| Splitting         A DmfA may be split into a maximum of 9 parts (SFTP manual v14 section 8.1). |
|  |
| ═══ BATCH FILE NAMING — NSSO SFTP MANUAL v14 SECTION 8 ═══ |
| FI.DMFA.<sender>.<YYYYMMDD>.<seq>.<env>.<parts>.<part> |
| FS.DMFA.<sender>.<YYYYMMDD>.<seq>.<env>.<parts>.<part> |
| GO.DMFA.<sender>.<YYYYMMDD>.<seq>.<env>.<parts> |
|  |
| Single part:      FI.DMFA.123456.20170213.00001.R.1.1 |
| FS.DMFA.123456.20170213.00001.R.1.1 |
| GO.DMFA.123456.20170213.00001.R.1 |
| Two parts:        FI.DMFA.123456.20170213.00001.R.2.1 |
| FI.DMFA.123456.20170213.00001.R.2.2 |
| FS.DMFA.123456.20170213.00001.R.2.1 |
| FS.DMFA.123456.20170213.00001.R.2.2 |
| GO.DMFA.123456.20170213.00001.R.2 |
|  |
| Environment codes are specific to DmfA and must not be confused: |
| R  production |
| T  circuit test — the full control circuit as in production, with worker identification |
| checks but no Sigedis identification check. Folder INTEST, results in OUTTEST. |
| A positive notification SAVES the declaration in the simulation environment, and the |
| circuit test is limited to one accepted declaration per NSSO-number / quarter pair. |
| S  declaration test — all reception and content controls, no worker identification check. |
| Folder INTEST-S, results in OUTTEST-S. Nothing is saved, so the same declaration can |
| be tested repeatedly. S exists for DmfA only; every other application uses T. |
|  |
| ═══ XML STRUCTURE — FUNCTIONAL BLOCK HIERARCHY WITH CARDINALITY ═══ |
| <Form>                                90059  [1..*]   envelope |
| <Reference>                         90082  [0..1] |
| <DmfAOriginal>                      90169  [1..1]   declaration type container |
| <EmployerDeclaration>             90007  [1..1]   EMPLOYER LEVEL — quarter, NSSO number, net payable |
| <ContributionUnrelatedToNP>     90002  [0..*]   employer-level contributions with no worker |
| <NaturalPerson>                 90017  [0..*]   the worker's identity |
| <Address>                     90022  [0..1] |
| <WorkerRecord>                  90012  [1..*]   WORKER LEVEL — one per employee per quarter, keyed on the INSZ |
| <Occupation>                  90015  [0..*]   OCCUPATION LINE — a new line per determining characteristic |
| <OccupationInformations>    90313  [0..1] |
| <ReorgMeasureInformation>   90438  [0..2] |
| <ActivationInformation>     90578  [0..1] |
| <Service>                   90018  [0..*]   days and hours per service code |
| <Remun>                     90019  [0..*]   gross per remuneration code |
| <OccupationDeduction>       90109  [0..*]   reductions at occupation level |
| <OccupationDeductionDetail> 90250 [0..1] |
| <WorkerContribution>          90001  [0..*]   base and amount per contribution type |
| <WorkerDeduction>             90110  [0..*]   reductions at worker level |
| <DeductionDetail>           90108  [0..99] |
| <CompanyVehicle>              90294  [0..*]   CO2 solidarity contribution, per vehicle |
| <StudentContribution>         90003  [0..1]   solidarity contribution |
| <EarlyRetirementContribution> 90042  [0..2] |
| <ComplementaryIndemnity>      90336  [0..*]   SWT / RCC |
| <ComplIndemnityContribution> 90337 [0..*] |
| <IndemnityWAPM>               90011  [0..*]   work accident and occupational disease |
| <EmployerCompensation>        90595  [0..1] |
| <UsingEmployer>               90107  [0..*]   temporary agency work |
|  |
| OUT OF SCOPE FOR THIS BUILD (public sector / provincial and local administration): |
| <DismissedStatutoryWorkerContribution> 90005 |
| <SecondPillarInformation>     90172 |
| <OccupationPublicServiceData> 90411 |
| <ScaleSalary>                 90412 |
| <AdditionalScaleSalary>       90413 |
|  |
| ═══ THE DISAGGREGATION MODEL IMPOSED ON PAYROLL — CCG MODULE 10.1 ═══ |
| The hierarchy above is not presentation: it is a set of requirements on the payroll engine. |
| A total that cannot be split along these axes cannot be declared. |
|  |
| Per employee, per quarter      gross by remuneration code; days and hours by service code |
| Per occupation line            a new line whenever the joint committee, worker code, |
| working regime or contract type changes mid-quarter |
| Per contribution type          the base AND the amount separately, never a net figure |
| Per reduction                  the reduction amount AND the parameters that justified it |
| Per vehicle                    the CO2 contribution, per month of availability |
| Per absence                    the correct service code, because it drives both benefit |
| entitlement and holiday accrual |
|  |
| ═══ RESPONSE LEGS ═══ |
| IN-02  DmfA validation report — anomalies, blocking and non-blocking. Anomalies must be |
| corrected before the deadline (CCG Module 10.2). |
| IN-03  NSSO contribution statement and advance notice — the advance amounts to pay and the |
| balance calculated by the NSSO. The advances are calculated by the NSSO, not by the |
| employer, so the engine must consume them rather than compute them. |

### Sheet: `Population Rules`

| Rule Category | Field Name | Source System | Population Logic | Edge Cases |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ═══ MANDATORY FIELD RULES ═══ |  |  |  |  |
| Declaration key | Year and Quarter (00013) | Payroll period control | Five positions, YYYYQ. This is the primary key of the declaration and it never changes for a correction: a modification declaration is always allocated to the ORIGINAL quarter at the rates and reductions of that quarter (CCG Modules 9.2 and 10.5), never to the quarter in which the error was found. The engine must therefore be able to re-open and re-run a closed quarter end to end rather than post a difference into the current one. | A quarter that has already produced a corrective declaration can produce another; there is no general deadline, but corrections beyond the three-year limitation period are subject to the prescription rules (CCG Module 10.5). |
| Identification | INSZ (00024) | Employee master data | The INSZ keys the worker block and must be identical to the number on the accepted Dimona for the same employment period. This is not a soft link: the DmfA is validated against the Dimona and a mismatch is a blocking rejection. Take the value from the stored employment record written when the Dimona acknowledgement (SIR IN-01) was received, never re-derive it from the employee master record, because a national register number corrected after the Dimona was accepted must be declared to the NSSO before it can be used here. | A worker holding a BIS number who later obtains a definitive national register number has two identities across a quarter boundary. The change must be sequenced through the identification channel first, otherwise the quarter cannot be declared under either number. |
| Employer level | Net Amount Payable (00015) | Payroll result | The total amount payable for the quarter, in eurocent, after every reduction. It is the arithmetic result of all contribution blocks less all deduction blocks and must reconcile exactly to the sum of the declared parts — the NSSO recomputes it. Do not populate it from a payroll control total computed on a different basis, because the two will differ on rounding. | Where monthly advances have been paid because the K-2 threshold of EUR 6,197.34 was exceeded, this zone still carries the full quarterly figure; the advances are settled separately and the NSSO calculates the balance. The advance amounts arrive on SIR IN-04 and are calculated by the NSSO, not by the employer. |
| ═══ CRITICAL VALIDATION RULES ═══ |  |  |  |  |
| Occupation line splitting | Occupation (90015) — 00044, 00045, 00046, 00037, 00050, 00048, 00049 | Contract master data | Open a NEW occupation line whenever any determining characteristic changes within the quarter: the worker code, the joint committee, the working-time regime, the contract type, or a start or end date (CCG Module 10.1). This is the single most common source of a structurally wrong DmfA, because payroll systems naturally hold one contract record per employee and the DmfA wants one line per homogeneous period. An employee promoted from part-time to full-time on 1 August in Q3 produces two occupation lines, each with its own service and remuneration blocks, not one line with an averaged regime. | A mid-quarter joint committee change also changes the sectoral CBA, the pay scales and potentially the worker code, so the split cascades into the contribution blocks. A retroactive change notified after the quarter closed requires a modification declaration (BE-NSSO-003), not an adjustment in the following quarter. |
| No netting | Contribution base (00084) vs amount (00085); deduction base (00088) vs amount (00089) | Contribution and reduction engines | CCG Module 10.1 states the general rule without qualification: no netting is permitted. Per contribution type the base and the amount are declared separately, never a net figure; per reduction the reduction amount and the parameters that justified it are declared separately from the contribution they reduce. Concretely, the social work bonus appears in a deduction block (90110) with its own base and amount, and the employee contribution in block 90001 is declared at its full pre-bonus value. CCG Module 10.1 lists 'employee contribution before and after the work bonus' as two distinct required intermediates for exactly this reason. | A payroll engine that stores only the post-reduction contribution cannot produce this declaration at all and must be changed rather than worked around. The same applies to the structural reduction and to every target-group reduction. |
| Amount format | All amount zones (00015, 00070, 00084, 00085, 00088, 00089, 00021, 00022, 00076, 00077, 01011) | Payroll result | Every amount is a numeric zone expressed in eurocent with an implied two-decimal scale and NO decimal separator: EUR 10,500.00 is transmitted as 1050000. A decimal point, a comma, a currency symbol or a thousands separator anywhere in an amount zone is a blocking anomaly. Negative values are permitted and are how a within-quarter regularisation is expressed; the sign convention follows the glossary's domain for each zone. | Rounding must be applied once, at the point the eurocent value is formed, and never twice. Where an amount is derived from a rate applied to a base, declare the base and the amount as they were actually computed — reconstructing one from the other at declaration time reintroduces a rounding difference the NSSO will detect. |
| Working time | Hours zones (00048, 00049, 00064, 01158) | Time and attendance | Hours are expressed in HUNDREDTHS of an hour, not in hours and minutes and not in decimal hours with a separator. The DRS glossary states the convention explicitly with a worked example: 7 hours 40 minutes is expressed as 766. A 38-hour week is 3800. This is the most frequently mis-implemented convention in the Belgian declaration set, because 7h40 looks like 7.40 and 7.40 hours is 740, which is wrong by 26 hundredths. | Zone 00064 (hours of the service) is mandatory for part-time occupations and for hours-based service codes, and optional for a full-time worker declared in days only. Declaring hours inconsistently across occupation lines of the same worker will not be rejected but will corrupt the benefit entitlement calculations downstream, because the DmfA is multifunctional and these hours feed the pension administration, the health insurance funds and the National Employment Office. |
| ═══ PAYROLL-SPECIFIC POPULATION RULES ═══ |  |  |  |  |
| Disaggregation | Remuneration Code (00067) and Remuneration (00070) | BE-WTC-001 wage types | Gross pay is never declared as a single figure. It is disaggregated into one Remun block per remuneration code, each carrying its own amount. Map every earning wage type in BE-WTC-001 onto a remuneration code and sum within the code. For blue-collar workers the contribution base is the gross at 108%, which CCG Module 10.1 lists as a required intermediate — the 108% uplift is applied to the base, not to the declared gross, and the two must be held separately in payroll. | The code values themselves are in NSSO Annexe 7, which is NOT held in 00-official-sources. This specification documents the five codes CCG Module 10.1 records (1 ordinary, 2 premiums not linked to a work period, 3 departure holiday pay, 4 benefits not calculated per period, 5 premiums for the quarter) and marks the codes for indemnities, arrears and blue-collar single holiday pay NOT FOUND. A developer cannot complete this mapping without the annexe. |
| Disaggregation | Service Code (00062), days (00063) and hours (00064) | Time and attendance, absence engine | Days and hours are disaggregated per service code. CCG Module 10.1 warns that the correct code matters twice over, because the service code drives both the benefit entitlement of the employee and the holiday accrual of the employer — an absence coded wrongly costs the employee a benefit and mis-states the holiday provision. Map every absence type in the time and attendance feed (SIR IN-12) onto a service code before summing. | The full absence code set is in NSSO Annexe 8, which is NOT held. Codes 1, 2, 3, 5, 10 and 12 are documented from CCG Module 10.1 and appear in the Field Options sheet; the rest are marked NOT FOUND. |
| Special contributions | Company Vehicle block (90294) — 00780, 00781, 01217 | Fleet data, SIR IN-10 | One block per vehicle, driving the CO2 solidarity contribution per month of availability. The contribution depends on the CO2 value, the fuel type and — critically — the ORDER DATE, which selects both the CO2 minimum contribution and the multiplier. The order date is not a payroll date and is not derivable inside payroll: it arrives from the leasing company on SIR IN-10 and must be stored per vehicle. | BE-SIR-001 gap G22 records that no published interchange format exists for fleet data at all: the only Renta standard is a vehicle return-condition standard, not an interchange format. The data contract must therefore be agreed per client and per leasing company, and the engine must fail loudly on a missing order date rather than defaulting it, because a defaulted order date silently produces the wrong contribution for the life of the vehicle. |
| Special contributions | Student Contribution block (90003) — 00076, 00077, 00078, 01158 | BE-WTC-001, Student@work SIR IN-05 | The solidarity contribution applies only while the student remains within the 650-hour annual quota. Zone 01158 declares the hours consumed in the quarter, in hundredths. Before declaring, reconcile against the Student@work counter, which reports hours already consumed across ALL employers, not only this client. Where the quota is exceeded, ordinary employee and employer contributions become due from the first hour of the excess, the worker code changes, and BE-WTC-001's wage type 'Requalification - student wage beyond the 650-hour annual quota [21148]' is the mechanism for the resulting correction. | The quota is consumed in declaration order across employers, so a competing employer's later declaration can retroactively push this client's student over the line — producing a correction to a quarter that was correct when filed. BE-SIR-001 gap G18 records that it is not published whether any batch or web-service channel exists for the quota consultation, so a high-volume student employer may be constrained to a web-only check. |
| ═══ CROSS-FIELD VALIDATIONS ═══ |  |  |  |  |
| Cross-declaration | DmfA occupation line vs the accepted Dimona period | SIR IN-01, BE-NSSO-001 | Every occupation line must fall inside an accepted Dimona period for the same INSZ and the same employer. The NSSO validates this and a rejected or missing Dimona blocks the quarterly declaration (CCG Module 10.1). The engine must run this check itself before submission rather than discovering it on the validation report, because the DmfA deadline is the last day of the month following the quarter and a Dimona correction plus a DmfA resubmission does not fit comfortably inside the remaining days. | A worker whose Dimona OUT was filed late, or not at all, will have an occupation line extending beyond the accepted Dimona period. Correct the Dimona first, then declare. |
| Cross-field | Contract Type (00050) vs worker hours (00048) and reference hours (00049) | Working-time configuration | Contract type 0 (full time) requires the worker's average weekly hours to equal the reference person's average weekly hours; type 1 (part time) requires them to differ. Both are expressed in hundredths of an hour. The pair also drives proration throughout payroll and the part-time thresholds in the reduction calculations, so an inconsistency here propagates into the deduction blocks rather than staying local. | A full-time worker in a sector whose reference week is not 38 hours must have the reference hours set from the joint committee, not from a system default. Zone 00049 is the sectoral full-time reference, not the company norm. |
| Cross-field | Deduction blocks (90109, 90110) vs their detail blocks (90250, 90108) | Reduction engine | A deduction block carries the code, base and amount; the detail block beneath it carries the parameters that justified the reduction — the sequence number, the detail amount, the work rules registration number, the date the entitlement originated, and the average weekly working time before and after a working-time reduction. CCG Module 10.1 requires both: 'the reduction amount AND the parameters that justified it'. A reduction claimed without its detail block is claimable but not defensible on inspection. | Block 90108 has cardinality [0..99] and 90250 has [0..1]; a reduction requiring more than one detail line must therefore sit at worker level (90110) rather than occupation level (90109). This constrains where a given reduction can be declared and is a structural decision, not a formatting one. |
| Cascade | Any corrected figure | Whole engine | CCG Module 10.5: corrections cascade. A corrective DmfA changes the quarterly wage, which can change the special social security contribution band and the social work bonus, which changes the net, which changes the taxable base and therefore the 281.10. The engine must be able to re-run the affected quarter end to end rather than patching a single figure, and the resulting changes must be pushed into BE-NSSO-003 (DmfA modification), BE-FIN-001 (withholding tax correction) and BE-FIN-002 (corrective 281.10) as a set. | The three correction routes have different deadlines and different authorities, so the cascade cannot be treated as a single transaction. For income year 2025 the withholding-tax correction windows closed on 15 May 2026 for exemption-related corrections and 10 July 2026 for others, with the Finprof channel for that income year closing on 31 August 2026, while a corrective DmfA has no general deadline. A correction found in September 2026 for income year 2025 can therefore still be made to the DmfA but no longer to the withholding tax return. |

Subject to the three-year prescription rules (CCG Module 10.5) | XML over SFTP or FTP, application code DMWA; or the 'Modify a declaration' function of the DmfA online service | XML | Law of 27 June 1969; Royal Decree of 28 November 1969 implementing it; the prescription rules on social security contributions | ACCURACY: HIGH ON SEMANTICS, INHERITED ON STRUCTURE — the correction rules in this document come directly from CCG Module 10.5 and the NSSO channel documentation, and the application code DMWA is taken verbatim from the SFTP user manual v14. CONFIDENCE NOTE: the field layout is inherited from BE-NSSO-002 and carries exactly the same limitation — NSSO Annexes 2, 3, 4, 7 and 8 are not held, so the coded fields cannot be populated from this document alone. One item is genuinely open and is NOT guessed: which attestation status values (zone 00110) the DMWA application accepts. The glossary lists nine values for the zone but does not state the subset valid for a modification, and no held source resolves it. |

### Sheet: `Payroll Scope Summary`

| DmfA Modification — PAYROLL SCOPE SUMMARY |  |  |
| --- | --- | --- |
|  |  |  |
| When a correction is made through this declaration rather than through some other route, and what the engine must be able to do to produce it. The governing rule is CCG Module 9.2 and 10.5: the corrective declaration restates the ORIGINAL quarter at the rates and reductions of that quarter. |  |  |
|  |  |  |
| ITEM / SCENARIO | IN SCOPE? | NOTES / REASONING |
| ═══ WHEN THIS DECLARATION IS THE CORRECT ROUTE ═══ |  |  |
| A wrong wage declared in a closed quarter | YES | CCG Module 10.5: social security — wrong wage, days or contribution is corrected by a corrective DmfA for the original quarter. |
| Wrong days or hours in a closed quarter | YES | Including a wrongly coded absence, which matters because the service code drives both benefit entitlement and holiday accrual. |
| A contribution or reduction wrongly computed | YES | The NSSO recalculates and issues a debit or a credit. |
| A retroactive joint committee or worker code change | YES | The occupation lines of the original quarter are restated with the corrected boundaries. |
| A student who exceeded the 650-hour quota because of a LATER declaration by another employer | YES | The quota is consumed in declaration order across all employers, so a quarter that was correct when filed can become wrong afterwards through no act of this client. |
| An error found before the original declaration was submitted | NO | Correct the original and submit once. A modification presupposes an accepted original. |
| An error in the CURRENT open quarter | NO | Adjust within the current quarter's original declaration. Amount zones accept negative values for a within-quarter regularisation. |
| A wrong wage withholding tax amount | NO | A different authority and a different channel — the withholding tax correction route (BE-FIN-001), which has its own published correction windows. |
| A wrong 281.10 amount | NO | A corrective filing through Belcotax-on-web (BE-FIN-002), which produces a corrected certificate for the employee. |
| A wrong Dimona period | NO | DimonaUpdate or DimonaCancel (BE-NSSO-001). Correct the Dimona FIRST — the DmfA is validated against it. |
| ═══ TIMING AND RELATIONSHIP ═══ |  |  |
| Allocated to the original quarter | YES | Never to the quarter of discovery. This is the defining rule of the declaration. |
| Applies the rates and reductions of the original quarter | YES | CCG Module 9.2. A 2024 correction filed in 2026 uses 2024 contribution rates, 2024 reduction parameters and 2024 thresholds — not current ones. |
| Subject to a filing deadline | NO | CCG Module 10.5 records no general deadline, but corrections beyond the three-year limitation period are subject to the prescription rules. |
| Triggers a cascade into other filings | YES | CCG Module 10.5: a corrective DmfA changes the quarterly wage, which can change the special social security contribution band and the social work bonus, which changes the net, which changes the taxable base and therefore the 281.10. |
| ═══ AMOUNTS AND CALCULATIONS ═══ |  |  |
| Amounts restated in full | YES | The corrected quarter is declared as it should have been. The NSSO computes the difference. |
| Difference amounts declared | NO | The employer does not compute or declare a delta. Declaring a delta produces a double correction once the NSSO applies its own. |
| The engine must be able to re-run a closed quarter end to end | YES | CCG Module 10.5 states this as a system requirement, not a preference: patching a single figure cannot produce a correct restatement because the corrections cascade internally. |
| ═══ SPECIAL CASES ═══ |  |  |
| A quarter corrected more than once | YES | Each modification restates the quarter afresh; there is no limit stated in the held sources. |
| An overpayment recovered from the employee | YES | CCG Module 10.5: recovered from net pay within the one-fifth cap of Article 23 of the Wage Protection Act, with the corresponding DmfA and 281.10 corrections. The employee repays the NET; the employer recovers the tax and contributions from the authorities. |
| Correction of a quarter beyond the three-year prescription period | NO | Subject to the prescription rules. Raise to the client rather than filing. |
| Splitting a large modification into parts | YES | The SFTP multi-part rules apply to DMWA as they do to DMFA — up to 9 parts. |

| NOSS Quarter Starting Date | DATE DE DÉBUT DU TRIMESTRE POUR LA SÉCURITÉ SOCIALE | WORKER RECORD — modification (90012) | Zone 00038 | Y | Y |  | /DmfAOriginal/WorkerRecord/NOSSQuarterStartingDate | 10 | AN(10) — format: AAAA-MM-JJ (YYYY-MM-DD) · AAAA is the year · MM is the month · JJ is the day | 2026-07-01 | Payroll period control — start of the quarter for social security. | Restated at its corrected value for the original quarter. Start date of the quarter covered by the declaration of the worker contract. This date may coincide with the first day (01/01, 01/04, 01/07, 01/10) of a calendar quarter (normal case for white-collar employees). ### Sheet: `File Structure`

| DmfA Modification — FILE STRUCTURE AND TECHNICAL SPECIFICATIONS |
| --- |
|  |
| ═══ FILE FORMAT ═══ |
| Format            XML, the SAME schema as the original DmfA declaration. |
| Encoding          NOT FOUND - requires direct inquiry to the NSSO (gap G1). |
| Transport         SFTP or FTP, application code DMWA. |
| Alternative       'Modify a declaration' (Modifier une déclaration) in the DmfA online service. |
| Splitting         Up to 9 parts, as for the original declaration. |
|  |
| ═══ BATCH FILE NAMING — THE ONLY STRUCTURAL DIFFERENCE FROM THE ORIGINAL ═══ |
| FI.DMWA.<sender>.<YYYYMMDD>.<seq>.<env>.<parts>.<part> |
| FS.DMWA.<sender>.<YYYYMMDD>.<seq>.<env>.<parts>.<part> |
| GO.DMWA.<sender>.<YYYYMMDD>.<seq>.<env>.<parts> |
|  |
| The NSSO SFTP user manual v14 section 8.1 lists the application codes: |
| DMFA  original DmfA declaration |
| DMWA  modification of a DmfA |
| DMRQ  consultation (request) of a DmfA |
|  |
| Everything else in the naming convention is identical to the original. |
|  |
| ═══ XML STRUCTURE ═══ |
| Identical to BE-NSSO-002 BELOW THE ROOT: the same functional blocks, the |
| same cardinalities, the same zone numbers, the same XML labels. The ROOT is the exception - block 90169 <DmfAOriginal> is the root of an ORIGINAL declaration only (glossary 2026/2); the modification root is NOT FOUND in any held source and has not been guessed. See sheets 'DmfA Modification Spec' A12 and 'Sample File'. |
|  |
| See BE-NSSO-002-DmfA-Spec.xlsx, sheet 'File Structure', for the full |
| hierarchy. It is not duplicated here, because duplicating it would create |
| two documents that can drift apart against one official glossary. |
|  |
| ═══ WHAT THE CORRECTION MUST RESTATE ═══ |
| The corrected quarter is declared as it SHOULD have been, in full: |
|  |
| every worker block that belongs in the quarter, not only the corrected worker |
| every occupation line of a corrected worker, not only the line that changed |
| every service and remuneration block beneath a corrected occupation line |
| every contribution block, at the rates of the ORIGINAL quarter |
| every deduction block, at the reduction parameters of the ORIGINAL quarter |
|  |
| The NSSO recalculates against the accepted original and issues a debit or a |
| credit for the difference. The employer neither computes nor declares it. |
|  |
| ═══ THE CASCADE — CCG MODULE 10.5 ═══ |
| A corrective DmfA does not stay inside social security: |
|  |
| corrective DmfA |
| -> changes the quarterly wage |
| -> can change the special social security contribution band |
| -> can change the social work bonus |
| -> changes the net |
| -> changes the taxable base |
| -> changes the 281.10  (BE-FIN-002, corrective Belcotax filing) |
| -> may change the wage withholding tax  (BE-FIN-001) |
|  |
| The three routes have different authorities and different deadlines, so the |
| cascade is not one transaction. A correction found in September 2026 for |
| income year 2025 can still be made to the DmfA — which has no general |
| deadline — but no longer to the wage withholding tax return, because the |
| Finprof channel for income year 2025 closed on 31 August 2026 (CCG 10.5). |

### Sheet: `Population Rules`

| Rule Category | Field Name | Source System | Population Logic | Edge Cases |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ═══ THE RESTATEMENT RULE — THE DEFINING RULE OF THIS DECLARATION ═══ |  |  |  |  |
| Restatement | Year and Quarter (00013) | Payroll period control | Populate with the ORIGINAL quarter, in the form YYYYQ. Never the quarter in which the error was found, and never the current quarter. CCG Module 10.5 is unambiguous: the correction route for a wrong wage, days or contribution is a corrective DmfA for the original quarter. A modification declaration bearing the current quarter is not a correction at all — it is a second original for a quarter that already has one, and it will collide. | A correction spanning several quarters produces several modification declarations, one per original quarter, each restating its own quarter. There is no multi-quarter correction declaration. |
| Restatement | All rate-dependent zones — 00084, 00085, 00088, 00089 | Contribution and reduction engines | Apply the rates, reduction parameters and thresholds of the ORIGINAL quarter, not the current ones (CCG Module 9.2). A 2024 quarter corrected in 2026 uses the 2024 contribution rates, the 2024 structural reduction parameters, the 2024 target-group reduction conditions and the 2024 wage thresholds. This means the engine must retain rate history indefinitely and must be able to select rates by declared quarter rather than by processing date — the single most common cause of a wrong corrective declaration is an engine that reaches for the current rate table. | Parameters that move DURING a year make this sharper still, and the two calendars must not be conflated (finding BE-X10-007). The GMMI itself moves on 1 January, 1 April and 1 August 2026 - there is no 1 July step. The social work bonus parameters, which are set as percentages of the GMMI, step FIVE times: 1 January, 1 March, 1 April, 1 July and 1 September 2026, with no 1 August row. BE-CCG-001 Module 5.1.1 carries the authoritative tables. A correction to a quarter that straddles any of those steps must apply the value in force on each date within the quarter, not the value at quarter end, and must select the work bonus row by the PAY MONTH. |
| Restatement | All amount zones | Payroll result | Declare the corrected FULL value, never a difference. The NSSO recalculates against the accepted original and issues a debit or a credit for the delta. An employer that declares the delta itself causes the NSSO to apply the delta twice — once as declared and once as computed — which produces a wrong balance that then has to be corrected by a further modification. | This is the opposite of the within-quarter convention, where a negative amount in an open quarter is a legitimate regularisation. The engine must therefore branch on whether the target quarter is open or closed, and must not treat a correction as 'a negative in the next period' under any circumstance. |
| ═══ SCOPE OF THE RESTATEMENT ═══ |  |  |  |  |
| Completeness | Worker blocks (90012) and occupation lines (90015) | Contract master data | Restate the corrected quarter in full: every worker block that belongs in the quarter and, for a corrected worker, every occupation line with its complete service, remuneration, contribution and deduction blocks. Restating only the changed line produces a quarter that is internally inconsistent, because the occupation lines of one worker partition the quarter between them and moving one boundary moves another. | A retroactive joint committee change is the clearest case: it splits one occupation line into two, which redistributes the service days and the remuneration between them, which changes the contribution base of each. None of that is visible if only the 'changed' field is restated. |
| Sequencing | Dimona period vs corrected occupation line | BE-NSSO-001, SIR IN-01 | Where the correction changes an occupation start or end date, check first whether the accepted Dimona period still covers it. If it does not, the Dimona must be corrected through DimonaUpdate BEFORE the modification declaration is filed, because the DmfA — original or modifying — is validated against the Dimona and a line outside the accepted period is a blocking rejection. | A worker whose employment end date moves backwards needs the Dimona OUT corrected first; one whose start date moves earlier may need a DimonaUpdate that the NSSO refuses because the original start has already passed. Establish the Dimona position before promising the client a corrected DmfA date. |
| ═══ CASCADE MANAGEMENT — CROSS-FILING ═══ |  |  |  |  |
| Cascade | Corrected quarterly wage | Whole engine | CCG Module 10.5: corrections cascade. A corrective DmfA changes the quarterly wage, which can change the special social security contribution band and the social work bonus, which changes the net, which changes the taxable base and therefore the 281.10. Re-run the affected quarter end to end and then determine, for each downstream filing, whether it too must be corrected — do not assume a social security correction is contained. | The special social security contribution is banded on the QUARTERLY gross, so a small wage correction near a band boundary produces a disproportionate change. The social work bonus depends on the reference monthly wage, so the same correction can change the bonus in one month of the quarter and not in the others. |
| Cascade | Downstream filings | BE-FIN-001, BE-FIN-002 | Where the corrected net or taxable base changes, raise the matching corrections: the wage withholding tax through the Finprof correction route (BE-FIN-001) and the annual certificate through a corrective Belcotax-on-web filing (BE-FIN-002), which produces a corrected certificate for the employee. Treat them as three separate obligations with three separate deadlines, not as one transaction. | The deadlines diverge sharply. A corrective DmfA has no general deadline. For income year 2025, withholding-tax corrections relating to exemptions had to be filed by 15 May 2026 and other corrections by 10 July 2026, and the Finprof channel for that income year closed on 31 August 2026 (CCG Module 10.5). A correction identified after those dates is still fileable to the NSSO and no longer fileable to FPS Finance — which must be raised with the client rather than absorbed. |
| Recovery | Overpayment to the employee | BE-WTC-001, payroll result | CCG Module 10.5: an overpayment is recovered from net pay within the one-fifth cap of Article 23 of the Wage Protection Act, with the corresponding DmfA and 281.10 corrections. The employee repays the NET amount; the employer recovers the tax and the contributions from the authorities through the corrective filings. Never recover the gross from the employee. | The one-fifth cap applies per pay period, so a large overpayment is recovered over several periods, each of which is a further payroll event in a later quarter, while the correction itself belongs to the original quarter. The two must not be confused: the recovery instalments are current-quarter events, the correction is an original-quarter restatement. |
| ═══ VALIDATION ═══ |  |  |  |  |
| Validation | Response legs IN-02 and IN-03 | SIR IN-02, IN-03 | A modification declaration returns the same validation report as an original: anomalies, blocking and non-blocking, which must be corrected before the deadline (CCG Module 10.2). Treat a modification as a full declaration for validation purposes — it is subjected to the same reception and content controls, and a modification can itself be rejected. | BE-SIR-001 gap G4 records that the NSSO has published no retry policy — no automatic retries, back-off, maximum attempts or idempotency guarantee — for any of its channels. A modification that appears to have been lost must therefore be investigated through consultation (DMRQ) before being resent, because resending is not known to be safe. |
| Testing | Environment code in the file name | Channel configuration | The DmfA-specific test environments apply to DMWA as they do to DMFA. Environment S (declaration test, folder INTEST-S) runs all reception and content controls with no worker identification check and saves nothing, so the same correction can be tested repeatedly. Environment T (circuit test, folder INTEST) runs the full circuit and SAVES a positively notified declaration in the simulation environment, limited to one accepted declaration per NSSO-number and quarter pair. | Because T saves, testing a correction twice in environment T for the same NSSO number and quarter will fail on the second attempt. Use S for iteration and T for a single final confirmation. |

### Sheet: `Example Analysis`

| DmfA Modification — EXAMPLE FILE ANALYSIS |  |  |  |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
|  |  |  |  |
| Raw Value | Field Name | Interpretation | Notes |
| ═══ THE CORRECTION KEY ═══ |  |  |  |
| 20243 | Year and Quarter (00013) | The ORIGINAL quarter — Q3 2024 — being corrected in 2026 | NOT the current quarter. The defining rule of this declaration. |
| DMWA | Application code (file name) | Identifies the file as a modification rather than an original | FI.DMWA.123456.20260814.00001.R.1.1 |
| 123456702 | NSSO Employer Registration Number (00011) | Unchanged from the original declaration | The correction is keyed on NSSO number plus quarter. |
| ═══ A WORKED CORRECTION — WAGE UNDERSTATED BY EUR 500.00 IN Q3 2024 ═══ |  |  |  |
| 1050000 | Remuneration (00070) — as originally declared | EUR 10,500.00 was declared | The accepted original. Shown for contrast only; it is not in the correction file. |
| 1100000 | Remuneration (00070) — as restated | EUR 11,000.00 is the corrected figure | The FULL corrected value, not the EUR 500.00 difference. |
| 1188000 | Calculation Base (00084) — as restated | EUR 11,880.00 — the corrected gross at 108% for a blue-collar worker | Recomputed at the 2024 basis, not at a current one. |
| 310508 | Contribution Amount (00085) — as restated | The contribution recomputed at the Q3 2024 RATE | CCG Module 9.2: the rates of the ORIGINAL quarter. |
| (not declared) | The difference | The NSSO recalculates and issues a debit or a credit | The employer neither computes nor declares the delta. |
| ═══ WHAT THE CORRECTION CASCADES INTO ═══ |  |  |  |
| Quarterly gross moves EUR 10,500 -> EUR 11,000 | Special social security contribution | The contribution is banded on the QUARTERLY gross, so a small move near a band boundary changes the band | CCG Module 10.5. |
| Reference monthly wage changes | Social work bonus | The bonus can change in one month of the quarter and not in the others | Declared as its own deduction block, never netted. |
| Net changes | Taxable base | Which changes the wage withholding tax and the 281.10 | Three filings, three authorities, three deadlines. |
| Income year 2025 correction found after 31 August 2026 | Finprof channel | Still fileable to the NSSO; no longer fileable to FPS Finance | CCG Module 10.5. Raise to the client rather than absorbing it. |

### Sheet: `Payroll Scope Summary`

| DRS / ASR — PAYROLL SCOPE SUMMARY |  |  |
| --- | --- | --- |
|  |  |  |
| Which social risks the payroll engine must declare, and what turns a correct payroll into a benefit the employee actually receives. BE-SIR-001 puts the stake plainly: without the correct mapping the employee receives no benefit. |  |  |
|  |  |  |
| ITEM / SCENARIO | IN SCOPE? | NOTES / REASONING |
| ═══ WHICH RISKS ARE DECLARED ═══ |  |  |
| Incapacity for work — sickness (ZIMA) | YES | Declared once the employer-funded guaranteed salary period ends and the health insurance fund takes over. The DmfA service code 5 (guaranteed salary during sickness) and the guaranteed-salary days in DmfA zone 01010 feed the calculation basis blocks of this declaration. |
| Maternity, birth, adoption and parental care (ZIMA) | YES | The same scenario family. DmfA service code 10 covers maternity leave. |
| Start of part-time work (WECH scenario 3) | YES | Zone 00430 always carries 001 in this scenario. It supports the income guarantee benefit for a worker moving to part-time work. |
| Unemployment, including the scenario that replaces the C4 | PARTIAL | In scope as an obligation, but the glossary for those scenarios is NOT held in 00-official-sources. Only scenario 3 is specified here. See the Field Options sheet. |
| Temporary unemployment (TWCT) | PARTIAL | In scope as an obligation — DmfA service code 12 is temporary unemployment — but the TWCT glossary is NOT held. Application code TWCT is confirmed from the SFTP manual; the field layout is not. |
| Work accident (AOAT) | NO | Not because it is out of scope, but because BE-SIR-001 registers it as its own outbound integration OUT-07. It is specified in BE-FEDRIS-001. |
| Provincial and local administration personnel (PPL blocks 90187, 90196, 90168) | NO | Out of scope for this build, consistent with BE-NSSO-002. The APL worker-code annex is not held. |
| Childminders (block 90407) | NO | A specific remuneration regime outside the scope of a general employer build. |
| ═══ TIMING AND RELATIONSHIP ═══ |  |  |
| Filed on the triggering event | YES | CCG Module 10.1. The recurring scenarios are monthly. |
| Fed by the DmfA service codes | YES | BE-SIR-001: the DmfA service codes and the employer-funded periods feed the scenarios. An absence coded to the wrong DmfA service code produces a wrong DRS and therefore a wrong or absent benefit — CCG Module 10.1 warns that the service code drives both benefit entitlement and holiday accrual. |
| Blocking the DmfA if omitted | NO | Unlike the Dimona, an omitted DRS does not block the quarterly declaration. It harms the employee, not the filing. |
| Returns an acknowledgement and a notification | YES | BE-SIR-001 records the direction as 'Both': an ACRF (accusé de réception) and a notification are returned. |
| Splittable into parts on the batch channel | NO | The SFTP manual is explicit: DRS and temporary unemployment declarations cannot be fractioned, so there is no seventh or eighth part in the file name. This is the opposite of the DmfA rule. |
| ═══ AMOUNTS AND CALCULATIONS ═══ |  |  |
| Carries a calculation basis for the benefit | YES | ZIMA scenario 1 devotes eight distinct blocks to it: the general basis (90032), the reference period (90405), part time (90013), overtime (90014), horeca overtime (90552), hours (90553), particular situations (90030) and particular remuneration methods (90406). This is where most of the payroll mapping work lies. |
| Hours expressed in hundredths of an hour | YES | The glossary states the convention with a worked example at zone 00102: 7 hours 40 minutes is expressed as 766, and the domain is the whole numbers 0 to 1400. |
| Carries the termination indemnity | YES | Block 90524. CCG Module 10.1 lists 'termination indemnity AND the period it covers' as a required payroll intermediate for both the 281.10 and the C4 — and the C4 is now this declaration family. |
| Carries benefits in kind | YES | Block 90029, benefits in kind and transfer indemnities, which enter the benefit calculation basis. |
| Computes the benefit itself | NO | The paying institution computes the benefit. Payroll supplies the basis, the working-time position and the absence classification. |
| ═══ SPECIAL CASES ═══ |  |  |
| A part-time worker's work schedule | YES | WECH scenario 3 blocks 90065 and 90037. The glossary constrains the schedule: where the working timetable is communicated it MUST take the form of exactly 1, 2, 3 or 4 weeks, and the permitted day indications for each length are in NSSO Annexe 34. |
| Return to work before the risk ends | YES | Block 90016 (Reprise du travail) in ZIMA scenario 1. |
| A relapse of the same incapacity | YES | Handled through the risk identification and risk detail blocks. CCG Module 8 governs the relapse rules and the guaranteed-salary consequences. |
| Declaration by paper | YES | Unusually for the Belgian set, the NSSO records that paper remains available for the DRS. It is not a route Mercans should use, but it means a failed electronic declaration is not an absolute bar to the employee's benefit. |

The complete domain, per BE-DD-001-v1.0 option mapper "Days Justification", is: 1 = Full-time worker, cycle beyond the quarter, MORE days worked than the average weekly regime provides 2 = Full-time worker, cycle beyond the quarter, FEWER days worked than the average weekly regime provides 3 = Part-time worker, cycle beyond the quarter, MORE days worked than the average weekly regime provides 4 = Part-time worker, cycle beyond the quarter, FEWER days worked than the average weekly regime provides 5 = Part-time worker, additional non-recoverable days. Part-time worker who, on top of the contractually-provided services, supplies a number of additional days in the quarter that cannot be recovered/offset later. 6 = Combination of 3+5 or 4+5. Combination of the situations described under codes 3 and 5, or under codes 4 and 5, within the same quarter. 7 = No services due for the quarter. ### Sheet: `File Structure`

| DRS / ASR — FILE STRUCTURE AND TECHNICAL SPECIFICATIONS |
| --- |
|  |
| ═══ FILE FORMAT ═══ |
| Format            XML, validated against the scenario's XSD in the NSSO TechLib. |
| Encoding          NOT FOUND - requires direct inquiry to the NSSO (gap G1). |
| Transport         SFTP or FTP on the social security extranet. |
| Alternative       The online service on the social security portal. |
| Alternative       Paper — the NSSO records that paper remains available for the DRS. |
|  |
| ═══ APPLICATION CODES — ONE PER SECTOR, FROM THE SFTP MANUAL v14 SECTION 8.1 ═══ |
| WECH   DRS 'Chômage' — unemployment declarations |
| ZIMA   DRS 'Indemnités' — indemnity declarations |
| AOAT   DRS 'Accidents du travail' — work accidents  (specified in BE-FEDRIS-001) |
| TWCT   Temporary unemployment declarations |
|  |
| File naming:  FI.<code>.<sender>.<YYYYMMDD>.<seq>.<env> |
| FS.<code>.<sender>.<YYYYMMDD>.<seq>.<env> |
| GO.<code>.<sender>.<YYYYMMDD>.<seq>.<env> |
|  |
| NOTE THE DIFFERENCE FROM THE DMFA: DRS and temporary unemployment declarations |
| CANNOT be split. The SFTP manual states this explicitly, so there is no seventh |
| part (total parts) and no eighth part (part number) in a DRS file name. The |
| manual's own examples make it plain: |
|  |
| FI.WECH.123456.20120213.00001.R          six name parts, no split |
| FI.AOAT.123456.20120213.00001.R          six name parts, no split |
| FI.DMFA.123456.20170213.00001.R.1.1      eight name parts, split permitted |
|  |
| Environment codes for DRS: R production, T test (folder INTEST). The DmfA-only |
| 'S' declaration-test environment does NOT apply — the manual states that for all |
| applications other than DmfA, only the T extension and the INTEST folder are used. |
|  |

| 'Déclaration de début de travail à temps partiel' |
| <NaturalPerson>               90017 |
| <Address>                   90022 |
| <ContactPerson>               90257 |
| <Communication>               90258 |

|  |
| ═══ THE WORK SCHEDULE CONSTRAINT — WECH SCENARIO 3 ═══ |
| The glossary constrains the work schedule at zone 00101: |
|  |
| Where the working timetable is communicated, it MUST take the form of exactly |
| 1, 2, 3 or 4 weeks. The permitted day indications for each of those lengths are |
| in NSSO Annexe 34 (Jours relatifs à la grille de travail), which is NOT held in |
| 00-official-sources. |
|  |
| And at zone 00102: |
|  |
| Hours per day of the schedule, whole numbers in the range 0 to 1400, expressed |
| in HUNDREDTHS OF AN HOUR. The glossary's own example: 7 hours 40 is 766. |
|  |
| A payroll system holding a rolling or averaged part-time schedule cannot declare |
| it here without first resolving it to a 1, 2, 3 or 4 week cycle. |
|  |
| ═══ RESPONSE LEGS ═══ |
| An ACRF (accusé de réception / ontvangstbevestiging) confirms reception and |
| carries the anomaly codes recorded per zone in column T of the spec sheet. |
| A notification is returned by the paying institution. |
|  |
| BE-SIR-001 gap G4 records that the NSSO publishes no retry policy for any of |
| its channels — no automatic retries, back-off, maximum attempts or idempotency |
| guarantee. A DRS that appears lost must therefore be investigated rather than |
| resent blind. |
