### Sheet: `Population Rules`

| Rule Category | Field Name | Source System | Population Logic | Edge Cases |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ═══ MANDATORY FIELD RULES ═══ |  |  |  |  |
| Scenario selection | Risk Identification (00430) | Payroll event engine | This three-digit zone tells the receiving institution which risk is being declared and therefore how to read the rest of the message. In WECH scenario 3 the glossary states it always carries 001. In ZIMA scenario 1 the permitted values are 001 to 008, whose individual meanings are in NSSO Annexe 12, which is not held. Select the value from the payroll absence event, never from an operator's free choice, and reject any event whose classification cannot be resolved to a permitted value rather than defaulting it. | The value is validated by the receiving institution and a wrong risk identification produces a declaration that is structurally accepted and functionally useless — the employee is assessed for the wrong benefit. The anomaly codes published for the zone (00430-001 not present, -002 non-numeric, -008 not in the definition domain, -093 incorrect length) are all blocking. |
| Identification | INSZ (00024) | Employee master data | The same INSZ used on the Dimona and the DmfA. The paying institution matches the declaration to the worker's social security record on this number, and it matches the declared occupation to the DmfA on it too. Take it from the stored employment record rather than re-deriving it. | The glossary records the INSZ as prohibited inside the UsingEmployer block (90107) — which appears in the work accident scenario rather than these two, but the rule is family-wide and an engine that populates the block generically will breach it. |
| Working time | Days indication (00101) and hours per day (00102) | Working-time configuration | For WECH scenario 3 the work schedule must be resolved into a fixed cycle before it can be declared: the glossary states that where the working timetable is communicated it MUST take the form of exactly 1, 2, 3 or 4 weeks, and that the permitted day indications for each cycle length are in NSSO Annexe 34. Hours per day go in zone 00102 in HUNDREDTHS of an hour, whole numbers in the range 0 to 1400 — the glossary's worked example is that 7 hours 40 minutes is 766. | A payroll system holding an averaged or rolling part-time schedule cannot declare it without first resolving it to one of the four permitted cycle lengths. Annexe 34 is not held, so the permitted day indications themselves cannot be stated in this specification and must be taken from the TechLib. |
| ═══ CRITICAL VALIDATION RULES ═══ |  |  |  |  |
| Cross-declaration | Service and remuneration blocks vs the DmfA | BE-NSSO-002, time and attendance | BE-SIR-001 states the dependency directly: the DmfA service codes and the employer-funded periods feed the DRS scenarios. The absence that triggers the declaration must carry the same service code here as it does in the DmfA, and the days and hours must agree. CCG Module 10.1 gives the reason the coding matters twice over — the service code drives both the benefit entitlement of the employee and the holiday accrual of the employer. | An absence coded wrongly is not caught by the channel, because both filings are internally consistent. It surfaces when the employee's benefit is refused or miscalculated, weeks later, by which time the DmfA quarter may be closed and a correction (BE-NSSO-003) is needed alongside a corrected DRS. |
| Guaranteed salary | Employer-funded period vs the start of the benefit | Absence engine, BE-NSSO-002 zones 01010 and 01011 | The declaration marks the boundary between the employer-funded guaranteed salary period and the period funded by the health insurance fund. The DmfA carries the employer side — zone 01010 the days of guaranteed salary in the first week and zone 01011 the gross remuneration paid during sickness — and this declaration opens the institutional side. Both must describe the same boundary date. | A relapse of the same incapacity within the period fixed by CCG Module 8 does not restart the guaranteed salary, so the boundary date of a relapse declaration is not the first day of the new absence. Getting this wrong either overpays the employer's guaranteed salary or leaves the employee with an unfunded gap. |
| Calculation basis | The eight calculation-basis blocks (90032, 90405, 90013, 90014, 90552, 90553, 90030, 90406) | BE-WTC-001, time and attendance | ZIMA scenario 1 devotes eight distinct blocks to the benefit calculation basis, and this is where most of the payroll mapping work for the DRS lies. Each addresses a different feature of the worker's remuneration — the general basis, the reference period, part-time work, overtime, horeca overtime specifically, hours, particular situations, and particular remuneration methods. Populate them from BE-WTC-001 wage types over the reference period the glossary defines in block 90077, not from the last pay period. | The horeca overtime basis (90552) exists as a separate block for the same reason the Belcotax fiche splits horeca overtime boxes: the sector's overtime regime differs, and CCG Module 4.4 records that a registered cash register raises the relief ceiling. A client in joint committee 302 needs this block; most clients do not. |
| No splitting | The batch file | Channel configuration | DRS and temporary unemployment declarations CANNOT be fractioned. The SFTP manual states it and its worked examples show it: a DRS file name has six parts (FI.WECH.123456.20120213.00001.R) where a DmfA has eight. An engine that applies the DmfA splitting logic generically to DRS files will produce names the channel rejects. | Only the T test environment and the INTEST folder apply. The DmfA-specific S declaration-test environment does not exist for DRS, so a DRS test declaration cannot be repeated freely the way a DmfA S test can. |
| ═══ PAYROLL-SPECIFIC POPULATION RULES ═══ |  |  |  |  |
| Termination | Termination indemnity block (90524) | BE-WTC-001, contract master data | CCG Module 10.1 lists 'termination indemnity AND the period it covers' as a required payroll intermediate, and names both the 281.10 and the C4 as its consumers. Since BE-SIR-001 records that unemployment scenario 1 REPLACES the C4 forms, the period the indemnity covers must be available to this declaration family, not only to the tax certificate. BE-WTC-001 carries the four indemnity wage types at Belcotax box 308 — notice, unfair dismissal under CBA no. 109, protection, and non-competition. | The covered period is what determines when unemployment benefit can begin, so an indemnity declared without its period leaves the employee unable to claim. The period is not derivable from the amount: it depends on the notice rules of CCG Module 9, not on a division by monthly salary. |
| Benefits in kind | Block 90029 | BE-WTC-001 | Benefits in kind and transfer indemnities enter the benefit calculation basis, so the same benefit-in-kind valuations that feed Belcotax zone 2.076 feed this declaration. Company car data comes from the fleet feed (SIR IN-10), which BE-SIR-001 gap G22 records as having no published interchange format at all. | A benefit in kind that is correctly valued for tax may need a different treatment for the benefit basis. Where the glossary's definition domain differs from the tax valuation, follow the glossary — this is a social security declaration, not a tax one. |
| Contact | Contact person and communication blocks (90257, 90258) | Provider configuration | These blocks carry the contact details the paying institution uses when it needs to resolve a query on the declaration. They are provider or client configuration rather than payroll values, but they are not decorative: a declaration that stalls on a query with no reachable contact leaves the employee without a benefit. | The contact is per declaration, not per client, so a client with several payroll administrators needs a rule for which one is named. |
| ═══ CROSS-FIELD VALIDATIONS ═══ |  |  |  |  |
| Cross-field | Contract type (00050) vs worker hours (00048) and reference hours (00049) | Working-time configuration | The same consistency rule as the DmfA: contract type 0 (full time) requires the worker's average weekly hours to equal the reference person's; type 1 (part time) requires them to differ. Both are in hundredths of an hour. In WECH scenario 3 this pairing is the substance of the declaration — it is precisely the move to part-time work that is being declared. | The reference hours are the SECTORAL full-time reference set by the joint committee, not the company norm. A client whose standard week is 40 hours in a sector whose reference is 38 must declare 38 in zone 00049. |
| Cross-field | Occupation dates (00044, 00045) vs the accepted Dimona period | BE-NSSO-001 | The occupation declared here must fall inside an accepted Dimona period for the same INSZ and employer. The DRS is not validated against the Dimona as strictly as the DmfA is, but the paying institution reconciles the worker's declared employment history across the chain, and an occupation outside the Dimona period will surface as a query rather than a rejection. | A worker whose Dimona OUT was filed late will have an occupation extending beyond the accepted period. Correct the Dimona before declaring the risk, not after. |
| Cross-filing | This declaration vs the DmfA quarter it falls in | BE-NSSO-002, BE-NSSO-003 | The absence declared here appears in the DmfA of the quarter it falls in, under its service code, with its days and hours. The two filings are made at different times — the DRS on the triggering event, the DmfA at the end of the quarter — so the DRS is usually filed first and the DmfA must be built to agree with it. | Where a correction to the absence is found after the quarter closed, BOTH must be corrected: a modification declaration for the DmfA (BE-NSSO-003) and a corrected DRS. They have different correction routes and neither triggers the other. |

| OUT OF SCOPE FOR HRBLIZZ - THE FILER IS A THIRD PARTY. The Limosa prior notification is filed by the FOREIGN posting employer or posted self-employed person, or their representative, before the posting starts. The Belgian host company is NEVER the filer. Legal basis: Programmawet (I) van 27 december 2006 / Loi-programme (I) du 27 decembre 2006, Title IV, Chapter VIII, art. 137 (scope), art. 139 (prior notification of posted workers), art. 141 (obligations of the end-user / principal) and art. 155 (posted self-employed persons), MB/BS 28 December 2006, executed by the Royal Decree of 20 March 2007; Social Criminal Code (level 3 sanction on the art. 141 duty). Independently confirmed against the NSSO's own Working in Belgium / Limosa portal, socialsecurity.be and Securex, which agree on the point. The posted population remains under its home social security scheme on an A1 portable document and is NOT processed through Belgian payroll at all - it stays on the home-country payroll for the duration of the posting - so this engine holds neither the obligation nor the source data. THE ONLY BELGIAN-SIDE DUTY IS NARROW AND EXCEPTION-BASED: art. 141 requires the person for whom the activities are carried out to verify that the declaration was made and to be able to produce the Limosa-1 acknowledgement of receipt, and to report the worker's identification data electronically to the NSSO ONLY WHERE THE LIMOSA-1 CANNOT BE PRODUCED. That is a document check at onboarding plus an exception report: it fires on a missing document, not on a pay run, carries no pay element, needs no payroll input and produces no payroll output. It is HR / onboarding scope, not payroll. ### Sheet: `Payroll Scope Summary`

| Limosa Declaration - PAYROLL SCOPE SUMMARY [DESCOPED - OUT OF SCOPE FOR HRBLIZZ] |  |  |
| --- | --- | --- |
|  |  |  |
| OUT OF SCOPE FOR HRBLIZZ - THE FILER IS A THIRD PARTY. The Limosa prior notification is filed by the FOREIGN posting employer or posted self-employed person, or their representative, before the posting starts. The Belgian host company is NEVER the filer. Legal basis: Programmawet (I) van 27 december 2006 / Loi-programme (I) du 27 decembre 2006, Title IV, Chapter VIII, art. 137 (scope), art. 139 (prior notification of posted workers), art. 141 (obligations of the end-user / principal) and art. 155 (posted self-employed persons), MB/BS 28 December 2006, executed by the Royal Decree of 20 March 2007; Social Criminal Code (level 3 sanction on the art. 141 duty). Independently confirmed against the NSSO's own Working in Belgium / Limosa portal, socialsecurity.be and Securex, which agree on the point. The posted population remains under its home social security scheme on an A1 portable document and is NOT processed through Belgian payroll at all - it stays on the home-country payroll for the duration of the posting - so this engine holds neither the obligation nor the source data. THE ONLY BELGIAN-SIDE DUTY IS NARROW AND EXCEPTION-BASED: art. 141 requires the person for whom the activities are carried out to verify that the declaration was made and to be able to produce the Limosa-1 acknowledgement of receipt, and to report the worker's identification data electronically to the NSSO ONLY WHERE THE LIMOSA-1 CANNOT BE PRODUCED. That is a document check at onboarding plus an exception report: it fires on a missing document, not on a pay run, carries no pay element, needs no payroll input and produces no payroll output. It is HR / onboarding scope, not payroll. RECORDED IN: scope_manifest.json out_of_scope entries BE-NSSO-LIMOSA-009 (the declaration) and BE-NSSO-LIMOSA-L1-VERIFY (the art. 141 check); BE-SIR-001-v1.0 Section 2.1 OUT-08, Section 1.1 IN-17 and Section 2.4; BE-CCG-001-v1.2 Modules 2.2, 10.1 and 11.2. THIS WORKBOOK IS RETAINED AS A DESCOPED RECORD AND IS NOT A BUILD TARGET. It is kept rather than deleted because it documents a real statutory obligation, records its own field-level gaps honestly, and is the evidence of why the obligation is out of scope; deleting it would destroy that record and leave the descoping unexplained. |  |  |
|  |  |  |
| ITEM / SCENARIO | COVERED BY THE LIMOSA OBLIGATION? | NOTES / REASONING. Column B answers whether the Limosa obligation covers the row - an obligation resting on the FOREIGN employer. It does NOT mean the row is in HRBLIZZ scope. Scope for this product is answered in the WHAT PAYROLL OWNS block below, where every answer is NO. |
| ═══ WHO THE FOREIGN EMPLOYER MUST DECLARE - reference only, none of this is filed by the Belgian payroll client ═══ |  |  |
| A worker posted into Belgium by a foreign employer | YES | The core case. The declaration is made before the worker starts. |
| A posted worker whose home scheme continues under an A1 | YES | CCG Module 11.2. The A1 is what keeps the worker out of Belgian social security; Limosa is what makes the posting visible to the Belgian authorities notwithstanding. |
| A worker active in several Member States | PARTIAL | CCG Module 11.2: applicable legislation is determined under Article 13 of Regulation (EC) 883/2004, with the 25% substantial-activity test. This is not a simple posting and the A1 rests on a different article, so the position must be established before deciding whether Limosa applies. |
| A non-EU national posted into Belgium | YES | And additionally a single permit — the combined work and residence authorisation issued by the region of employment (CCG Module 11.2). A separate obligation, driven by the same data. |
| An employee hired directly onto a Belgian contract | NO | That is a Dimona (BE-NSSO-001) and a DmfA (BE-NSSO-002), not a Limosa. The distinction is the posting, not the nationality. |
| A posted worker with NO A1 | NO | If the home scheme does not continue, the worker falls under Belgian social security and the ordinary Dimona plus DmfA chain applies. Establish the A1 position before choosing the route. |
| A frontier worker | NO | CCG Module 11.2 treats frontier workers under treaty-specific rules with their own tolerance thresholds for homeworking days. Not a posting. |
| ═══ WHAT PAYROLL OWNS - NOTHING. EVERY ANSWER IN THIS BLOCK IS NO ═══ |  |  |
| Assignment and identity master data | NO | CHANGED AT v1.3 - previously YES. The engine does not build this declaration, so there is no extract to own. BE-SIR-001 OUT-08 records product mapping as false and v1.3 of that register states why: not 'false because it is a master-data extract', which conceded the wrong point, but false because the payroll engine does not produce the flow at all. The assignment and identity data sits with the foreign posting employer, which is the declarant. |
| Any wage type mapping | NO | Unchanged, and now for the stronger reason: no wage-type mapping arises because the engine does not produce the declaration. Not one field in this specification is a pay element. |
| Storing the Limosa-1 receipt | NO | CHANGED AT v1.3 - previously YES, on the reasoning that the Belgian client must verify the receipt. The duty is real (art. 141) but it is not this product's. The Limosa portal returns the Limosa-1 to the FOREIGN declarant, in that declarant's own authenticated session; the Belgian side sights the copy the posted worker presents. That is a physical or PDF document check at onboarding, owned by HR, and it is descoped as BE-NSSO-LIMOSA-L1-VERIFY. scope_manifest.json accordingly no longer carries a BE-IN-LIMOSA-RECEIPT inbound integration. |
| Tracking the A1 validity against the posting period | NO | CHANGED AT v1.3 - previously YES. Not owned here for Limosa purposes, because the posting and its A1 live outside this payroll. The A1 matters to this build in one way only, and it is worth stating: it is the switch that decides whether the worker is on Belgian payroll AT ALL. If the A1 lapses or was never valid, the home scheme stops covering the worker, Belgian social security applies, and the ordinary Dimona plus DmfA chain begins - at which point the worker enters this engine as a normal Belgian-payroll population and Limosa ceases to be the governing route. Tracking A1 validity against a posting period is HR's; reacting to its lapse is payroll's. |
| ═══ TIMING AND RELATIONSHIP ═══ |  |  |
| Filed before the posted worker starts | YES | CCG Modules 10.1 and 11.2. A prior declaration: there is no post-hoc filing route, unlike a late Dimona which is an offence but still fileable. FILED BY THE FOREIGN EMPLOYER - the deadline binds that party, and appears on no calendar of this build (BE-SIR-001 Section 6.1 records the same). |
| Triggers the Checkinatwork presence obligation | YES | BE-SIR-001 records that Checkinatwork (OUT-18) applies to posted-worker presences under Limosa, alongside construction and the meat sector. OUT-18 is out of scope for this build, but the trigger must be raised. |
| Replaces the Dimona | YES | For a posted worker under an A1. The two are alternatives, not cumulative. This is the one line of this sheet with a direct consequence for the Belgian payroll team, and it is a NEGATIVE instruction: for a properly posted worker, do not expect and do not raise a Dimona, and do not treat the absence of one as a defect. |
| Produces a DmfA obligation | NO | Not where the home scheme continues under an A1. Contributions are due in the home state. |
| ═══ SPECIAL CASES ═══ |  |  |
| A posting extended beyond the declared end date | YES | The declaration must be amended BY THE FOREIGN EMPLOYER, and the A1 validity must be checked against the new end date. The published sources do not describe the amendment route - see the Field Options sheet. Relevant to this build only through row 18: an extension that outruns the A1 moves the worker into Belgian social security and therefore into this payroll. |
| A foreign employer with no Belgian establishment | YES | CCG Module 2.2: it registers with the NSSO as a foreign employer and may appoint a representative. The representative, where appointed, is a field of this declaration. |
| High-volume posting clients | PARTIAL | A web-only declaration is an operational constraint FOR THE FOREIGN EMPLOYER. The technical channel exists but its message layout is not published, so bulk filing cannot be designed from public sources. No longer an item for this implementation contract, since the filing is out of scope; retained because a client that is itself a posting entity would meet it. |

### Sheet: `File Structure`

| Limosa Declaration — FILE STRUCTURE AND TECHNICAL SPECIFICATIONS |
| --- |
|  |
| ═══ FILE FORMAT — WHAT IS AND IS NOT PUBLISHED ═══ |
| Format            NOT FOUND. CCG Module 10.1 records the format as 'Web'. |
| BE-SIR-001 Section 2.2 records it as 'Web declaration on the Limosa |
| portal, returning the Limosa-1 receipt'. |
| No message layout, XSD, field list or record description was found. |
| Encoding          NOT FOUND - not published. |
| Record length     NOT FOUND - not published. |
| Size limits       NOT FOUND - not published. |
|  |
| This is a confirmed absence rather than an unfinished search: BE-SIR-001 Section 8 |
| catalogues 21 authority-level gaps closeable by direct inquiry, and it does not |
| record a Limosa message layout as existing-but-unobtained. It records the channel |
| and its authentication, and nothing about a file. |
|  |
| ═══ THE TECHNICAL CHANNEL — WHAT BE-SIR-001 DOES ESTABLISH ═══ |
| Authentication    A GlobalSign certificate and a technical user, requested through the |
| secure-access request form for the social security portal. |
| (BE-SIR-001 Sections 3.3 and 3.4.) |
|  |
| Source status     BE-SIR-001 flags this explicitly: the GlobalSign-plus-technical-user |
| statement comes from the Working in Belgium portal, which is |
| government-operated but is a GUIDANCE PAGE rather than a technical |
| specification. It is 'treated as confirmed for planning, to be |
| re-verified at implementation'. |
|  |
| The same certificate-and-technical-user arrangement covers the OUT-18 Checkinatwork |
| technical channel, which is relevant because Checkinatwork applies to posted-worker |
| presences under Limosa. |
|  |
| ═══ DERIVED LOGICAL STRUCTURE — THIS DOCUMENT'S OWN GROUPING, NOT THE AUTHORITY'S ═══ |
| The six sections below are how this specification organises the requirements the |
| CCG and the SIR establish. They are NOT an authority-published record structure |
| and no claim is made that the real declaration is organised this way. |
|  |
| DECLARING PARTY          LIM-001 .. LIM-003   who files, and how they authenticate |
| FOREIGN EMPLOYER         LIM-010 .. LIM-014   the posting undertaking, and its |
| Belgian representative if any |
| POSTED WORKER            LIM-020 .. LIM-025   identity and nationality |
| THE POSTING              LIM-030 .. LIM-034   dates, place, nature of the services |
| BELGIAN CLIENT           LIM-040 .. LIM-042   the user of the services |
| SOCIAL SECURITY POSITION LIM-050 .. LIM-053   the A1 and the multi-state position |
| RECEIPT                  LIM-060              returned, not sent |
|  |
| ═══ WHAT MUST BE OBTAINED BEFORE THIS CAN BE BUILT ═══ |
| 1  The authority's own field identifiers, in place of the DERIVED LIM-nnn codes. |
| 2  Field lengths and data types. |
| 3  The code tables — at minimum for nationality, country, declarant type and the |
| nature of the services. |
| 4  Whether a machine channel accepts a structured message at all, and if so its |
| layout and its XSD. |
| 5  The amendment and cancellation routes for a posting whose dates change. |
| 6  Whether any bulk or batch route exists for a high-volume posting client. |
|  |
| Route: direct inquiry to the NSSO, or to the operator of the Working in Belgium |
| portal. This matches the pattern of BE-SIR-001 Section 8.1, where each gap carries |
| the enquiry that would close it and the party to ask. |
|  |
| ═══ RESPONSE LEG ═══ |
| The Limosa-1 receipt is returned on an accepted declaration (BE-SIR-001 Section 2.1, |
| direction 'Both'). It is not a technical acknowledgement: the Belgian client for whom |
| the services are performed must be able to verify that it exists before allowing the |
| work to begin, so it is a compliance artefact with a retention requirement. |
|  |
| Its format, length and structure are NOT FOUND. |

### Sheet: `Population Rules`

| Rule Category | Field Name | Source System | Population Logic | Edge Cases |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ═══ THE ROUTING DECISION — MADE BEFORE ANY FIELD IS POPULATED ═══ |  |  |  |  |
| Routing | Limosa vs Dimona plus DmfA | Assignment master data, A1 administration | Establish the social security position BEFORE choosing the declaration route, because the two routes are alternatives and the wrong one is not a formatting error but a missed statutory filing. CCG Module 11.2: a worker posted into Belgium whose home social security scheme continues under an A1 is declared through Limosa and is NOT subject to Belgian social security. A worker with no A1 falls under Belgian social security and needs the ordinary chain — Dimona before the start (BE-NSSO-001) and a quarterly DmfA (BE-NSSO-002). A worker active in several Member States is a third case again: applicable legislation is determined under Article 13 of Regulation (EC) 883/2004 with the 25% substantial-activity test, and the answer may be Belgium. | The A1 is often applied for but not yet issued when the posting starts. An assignment proceeding on an expected A1 that is later refused converts retroactively into a Belgian social security liability with a missing Dimona and missing DmfA quarters. The engine should treat 'A1 pending' as a distinct state and escalate it, not as an A1. |
| Routing | Multi-State Activity Indicator (LIM-053) | Assignment master data | Where the worker pursues activity in more than one Member State, CCG Module 11.2 applies Article 13 of Regulation (EC) 883/2004 with the 25% substantial-activity test rather than the simple posting rule. The A1 in that case rests on a different article and covers a different arrangement. Capture the multi-state position at assignment set-up, not at declaration time, because it changes which A1 is applied for. | The 25% test is measured on working time or remuneration in the state of residence. A worker who drifts across the threshold during an assignment changes applicable legislation, which changes everything downstream. It is not a set-and-forget field. |
| ═══ MANDATORY FIELD RULES — SUBJECT TO THE DERIVED CAVEAT ═══ |  |  |  |  |
| Timing | Posting Start Date (LIM-030) | Assignment master data | The declaration must be made BEFORE the posted worker starts (CCG Modules 10.1 and 11.2). This is a prior declaration and, unlike the Dimona, no post-hoc filing route is described in any held source: a late Dimona is an offence but is still fileable, whereas a Limosa filed after the start may leave the posting simply undeclared. Treat the start date as a hard gate in the assignment workflow, not as a data field. | The obligation is two-sided. The Belgian client for whom the services are performed must verify that the Limosa-1 receipt exists before allowing the work to begin, so a late declaration exposes the client as well as the employer. Where the start date moves earlier, the declaration must be made earlier — the receipt does not travel forward. |
| Identification | Foreign Employer Registration Number (LIM-013) and Belgian Representative (LIM-014) | Employer master data | The registration quoted here is the employer's registration in its HOME state, not a Belgian enterprise number. CCG Module 2.2 records that a foreign employer without a Belgian establishment registers with the NSSO as a foreign employer — a separate act producing a separate number, in the NSSO's own 9- or 12-position format with a two-digit modulo-97 check — and that where it has no Belgian presence it MAY appoint a representative. Because the appointment is optional, LIM-014 is conditional on the employer's Belgian presence rather than universally mandatory. | A foreign employer that acquires a Belgian establishment during a long posting changes category: it ceases to be a foreign employer without Belgian presence, and its representative arrangement may lapse. The declaration data is not static across a multi-year posting. |
| Identification | Belgian Client Enterprise Number (LIM-041) | Assignment master data | The KBO/BCE enterprise number of the Belgian client, in the format CCG Module 2.2 records: 10 digits presented as 0nnn.nnn.nnn, the first digit 0 or 1, and the last two digits a modulo-97 check on the preceding eight. Validate the check digits before submission. This is one of the few fields in this specification whose FORMAT is genuinely sourced, even though its identifier is not. | Where the Belgian client is a natural person rather than an undertaking there is no enterprise number. The held sources do not describe that case. |
| ═══ THE A1 — THE FIELD SET MOST LIKELY TO GO WRONG ═══ |  |  |  |  |
| Consistency | A1 validity (LIM-052) against the posting period (LIM-030, LIM-031) | A1 administration | The A1 validity period must cover the whole declared posting period. This is the pairing most likely to fall out of step, because postings are extended informally and A1s are not: an assignment quietly extended by six weeks past the A1 expiry leaves the worker with no home-state affiliation for those weeks, which means Belgian social security applies retroactively — a Dimona that was never filed, DmfA quarters that were never declared, and contributions that were never paid. Build the comparison as a standing check over the assignment, re-evaluated whenever either date moves, not as a one-off validation at declaration time. | The A1 is issued by the home Member State's institution and cannot be extended by the Belgian side. Where the extension request is refused or is still pending at the old expiry date, the correct answer is that Belgian social security applies from that date — and that must be escalated rather than assumed away. |
| Consistency | A1 presence (LIM-050) against the routing decision | A1 administration | LIM-050, LIM-051 and LIM-052 are conditional as a set: all three are present or none is. Where none is present, the worker is not on the Limosa route at all and the declaration should not have been made. The conditional group is therefore also a routing check. | A worker whose A1 rests on Article 13 (multi-state activity) rather than on the posting article carries an A1 that looks the same but certifies something different. LIM-053 is what distinguishes them and it must be captured, not inferred from the A1's existence. |
| ═══ DOWNSTREAM CONSEQUENCES ═══ |  |  |  |  |
| Retention | Limosa-1 Receipt Number (LIM-060) | Document management | The receipt is returned on an accepted declaration and is the evidence the Belgian client must be able to verify before allowing the work to begin. Store it against the assignment and make it retrievable on demand; a log line is not sufficient. Its format is NOT FOUND, so store it as received rather than parsing or reformatting it. | BE-SIR-001 Section 8 records no retention period for Limosa receipts, and CCG Module 2.3 governs retention generally. Apply the general rule until the specific one is obtained. |
| Trigger | Place of Work in Belgium (LIM-032) | Assignment master data | The place of work determines whether the Checkinatwork presence registration obligation arises. BE-SIR-001 Section 2.1 records that electronic presence registration is mandatory in construction and in the meat sector AND for posted-worker presences under Limosa — so for a posted worker the trigger can come from the posting itself, not only from the sector. OUT-18 is out of scope for this build, but the trigger must be raised to the client rather than passing silently. | The Checkinatwork REST service accepts up to 200 presences per request in its registerInBulk method (BE-SIR-001 Section 2.2), which is the only capacity figure published anywhere in that channel. It matters if a posting client later brings OUT-18 into scope. |
| Trigger | Worker Nationality (LIM-023) | Employee master data | A non-EU national posted into Belgium additionally requires a single permit — the combined work and residence authorisation issued by the region of employment (CCG Module 11.2). That is an HR obligation rather than a payroll filing, and it is issued by a REGION, so the region of employment must be established. The same nationality field drives both this declaration and that permit. | The region of employment is not always the region of the client's registered seat. A posting to a site in Wallonia for a client headquartered in Flanders is a Walloon permit. |

### Sheet: `Example Analysis`

| Limosa Declaration — EXAMPLE FILE ANALYSIS |  |  |  |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
|  |  |  |  |
| Raw Value | Field Name | Interpretation | Notes |
| ═══ A WORKED POSTING — WHAT THE VALUES MEAN ═══ |  |  |  |
| LIM-030 = 2026-09-01 | Posting Start Date | The posted worker starts on 1 September 2026 | The declaration must be made BEFORE this date. No post-hoc route is described in any held source. |
| LIM-031 = 2026-12-15 | Posting End Date | The posting is expected to end on 15 December 2026 | An extension requires the declaration to be amended AND the A1 validity to be rechecked. |
| LIM-052 = 2026-09-01 to 2026-12-31 | A1 Validity Period | The A1 covers the whole declared posting, with two weeks to spare | This is the pairing most likely to go wrong. An informal extension past 31 December moves the worker into Belgian social security retroactively. |
| LIM-041 = 0123.456.749 | Belgian Client Enterprise Number | The Belgian client, 10 digits as 0nnn.nnn.nnn | COMPOSITE: last two digits are a modulo-97 check on the preceding eight. This FORMAT is sourced from CCG Module 2.2 even though the field identifier is not. |
| LIM-024 = (none) | Worker INSZ or BIS Number | The posted worker has no Belgian social security number | The normal case. Where a BIS number exists from an earlier posting it should be quoted so the posting attaches to the existing record. |
| LIM-053 = false | Multi-State Activity Indicator | A simple posting, not Article 13 activity in several Member States | If true, applicable legislation is determined under Article 13 with the 25% substantial-activity test and the answer may be Belgium. |
| LIM-060 = (returned) | Limosa-1 Receipt Number | Returned by the authority on acceptance | Must be STORED and retrievable: the Belgian client must verify it exists before allowing work to begin. |
| ═══ WHAT THIS ANALYSIS CANNOT SHOW, AND WHY ═══ |  |  |  |
| (no raw record) | Field positions | No official field identifier exists for any field in this declaration | The LIM-nnn codes are this document's own. They are placeholders for the authority's identifiers, not a rendering of them. |
| (no raw record) | Field lengths and types | NOT FOUND in every case | No length, type, padding or justification rule is published. |
| (no raw record) | Code values | NOT FOUND in every case | Not even the nationality and country code lists are published for this declaration. The NSSO uses five-position NIS codes elsewhere; assuming the same here would be an assumption, not a source. |
| (no raw record) | A parsed sample | Impossible to produce honestly | A sample record would require inventing a layout. See the Sample File sheet. |
| ═══ THE ROUTING DECISION IN THREE CASES ═══ |  |  |  |
| A1 present, single Member State | Route: LIMOSA | The home scheme continues; no Belgian social security | CCG Module 11.2. Declare here; no Dimona, no DmfA. |
| No A1 | Route: DIMONA + DMFA | Belgian social security applies | BE-NSSO-001 before the start, BE-NSSO-002 quarterly. Limosa is not the route. |
| Activity in several Member States | Route: DETERMINE FIRST | Applicable legislation under Article 13 of Regulation (EC) 883/2004, 25% substantial-activity test | The answer may be Belgium. Do not default to Limosa. |
| A1 applied for but not yet issued | Route: ESCALATE | Neither route is safe | A refused A1 converts the posting retroactively into a Belgian liability with a missing Dimona and missing DmfA quarters. Treat as a distinct state. |

| Response         The Limosa-1 receipt. Format, length and structure NOT FOUND. |

| #ERROR! |
|  |
| 1  Whether the technical channel accepts a structured message at all, or whether |
| the certificate-and-technical-user arrangement only authenticates a portal |
| session. |
| 2  If a structured message exists: its schema, element names and namespace. |
| 3  Field lengths, data types, padding and justification. |
| 4  The code tables for nationality, country, declarant type and nature of services. |
| 5  The amendment and cancellation routes for a posting whose dates change. |
| 6  The format and structure of the Limosa-1 receipt. |
| 7  Whether any bulk or batch route exists for a high-volume posting client. |

|  |
| This matches the pattern of BE-SIR-001 Section 8.1, where every NOT FOUND carries |
| the enquiry that would close it and the party to ask. A gap in that list is a known |
| unknown with an owner, not an omission. |
|  |
|  |
| #ERROR! |
|  |
| The complete set of data the declaration must carry, as far as BE-CCG-001-v1.2 and |
| BE-SIR-001-v1.0 establish it — 24 fields across six logical sections, each with its |
| source named in column M, its conditionality reasoned in column G, and its |
| relationship to the A1, to Dimona, to the DmfA and to Checkinatwork stated. |
|  |
| That is enough to design the assignment data model and the intake process. |
| It is not enough to write the file, and it does not pretend to be. |

### Sheet: `Payroll Scope Summary`

| Wage Withholding Tax Return, form 274 — PAYROLL SCOPE SUMMARY |  |  |
| --- | --- | --- |
|  |  |  |
| What the withholding tax return carries and what it does not. The return is an EMPLOYER-LEVEL aggregate per income nature and per collection office — it names no employee. CCG Module 10.1 places it as a SEPARATE filing from the DmfA, with a different authority and on a different cycle. |  |  |
|  |  |  |
| ITEM / SCENARIO | IN SCOPE? | NOTES / REASONING |
| ═══ WHAT GETS REPORTED ═══ |  |  |
| Aggregate taxable base and withholding per income nature | YES | One SingleDeclaration per combination of District, Office, Language, ReferenceNumber, Year, Period, Year325 and RevenuNature. |
| Withholding exemptions for overtime, shift and night work, student work | YES | BE-SIR-001: the return reports the exemptions claimed SEPARATELY from the ordinary withholding. It does so by declaring them under their own income-nature code (06 shift and night premiums; 44 and 45 overtime; the scientific research codes 05, 07, 09, 31, 32, 33) in their own SingleDeclaration. |
| Company directors' remuneration | YES | Income nature 20, where the client pays directors through payroll. |
| Negative amounts — a regularisation | YES | Both TaxableRevenu and Prepayment accept a leading minus sign. Where several SingleDeclaration elements share all eight sort keys, the positive Prepayment amounts must PRECEDE the negative ones. |
| Individual employee names or identifiers | NO | Not one field in the return identifies an employee. The per-employee position is reported annually on the 281.10 (BE-FIN-002), which is why the two must be reconciled rather than derived from one another. |
| Social security contributions | NO | A different authority entirely. The DmfA (BE-NSSO-002) carries them. |
| Roerende voorheffing (withholding tax on movable income, form 273) | NO | A different tax and a different return. See the Version Control remark on the mislabelled source file — its code numbers must never be mapped into RevenuNature. |
| ═══ TIMING AND RELATIONSHIP ═══ |  |  |
| Filed separately from the DmfA | YES | CCG Module 10.1 filing-mechanics table, control C4: a different authority, a different cycle. |
| Generates the annual 281.10 | NO | CCG Module 10.1 is explicit and states it twice: the Belcotax annual filing is NOT generated from the twelve monthly withholding tax returns. It is an independent filing built from the payroll ledger, and it must be reconciled against them. |
| Reconciled against the payroll ledger at year end | YES | CCG Module 10.5 step 3: reconcile the twelve monthly returns against the payroll ledger in January. Note this is a reconciliation of what was DECLARED against what was PAID — there is no annual tax reconciliation in Belgian payroll and no recomputation of the employee's tax. |
| Paid on the same date as the return | YES | OUT-11, the SEPA payment of the withholding tax, carries the 12-digit PaymentReference specified in this return. |
| ═══ AMOUNTS AND CALCULATIONS ═══ |  |  |
| Amounts in eurocent with no decimal separator | YES | Both TaxableRevenu and Prepayment, at most 13 digits each. |
| Negative amounts signed with a LEADING minus | YES | The specification states the minus sign is placed BEFORE the amount, not trailed and not encoded in an overpunch. |
| Control totals computed by the sender | YES | PositiveDeclarations and NegativeDeclarations each carry a count and a total; OfficeAmount carries the number of collection offices in the file. The positive total can never be negative and the negative total must always be negative. |
| Employee-level tax recomputed | NO | CCG Module 10.5: there is no annual tax reconciliation in payroll. The employee settles through the personal income tax return. |
| ═══ SPECIAL CASES ═══ |  |  |
| The 'first 15 days of December' advance | YES | Period code 1215, for parties liable declaring more than EUR 2,500,000.00. A distinct period value, not a variant of 1200. |
| Filing through a recognised social secretariat | YES | SecretariatCode carries the secretariat's code; where there is none the value 9998 is placed in the zone rather than leaving it empty. CCG Module 10.4: this is an approval of the service provider, not of the software, and it is optional. |
| Correction after the income year has closed | PARTIAL | Correction windows are published and they close. For income year 2025, corrections relating to withholding exemptions had to be filed by 15 May 2026 and other corrections by 10 July 2026, and the Finprof channel for that income year closed on 31 August 2026 (CCG Module 10.5). After that the DmfA can still be corrected but this return cannot. |
| A year older than current year minus two | NO | Year permits the current year, minus one and minus two, the last only until that year is definitively closed. |

### Sheet: `File Structure`

| Wage Withholding Tax Return, form 274 — FILE STRUCTURE AND TECHNICAL SPECIFICATIONS |
| --- |
|  |
| ═══ FILE FORMAT ═══ |
| Format            XML. |
| Schema            Finprof.xsd — stated by name in the file description. |
| Encoding          ISO-8859-1 (ISO Latin 1) — stated explicitly. Unusually for the Belgian |
| statutory set, this encoding IS published; the DmfA and Belcotax are not. |
| Communication     The CoreHeader is imposed by the UME2 communication standard. |
| Alternative       Online entry in the FinProf application. |
| Size limit        NOT FOUND - requires direct inquiry to info.finprof@minfin.fed.be |
| (BE-SIR-001 gap G10). |
|  |
| ═══ XML STRUCTURE ═══ |
| <Declaration274 CreationDate="EEJJ-MM-DD"> |
| <CoreHeader> |
| <MessageType>REQUEST</MessageType>                 imposed by UME2 |
| <Origin>FINPROF</Origin> |
| <DocumentType>Multiple_PRP_Declaration</DocumentType> |
| </CoreHeader> |
| <Declaration> |
| <LastPeriod>JJMM</LastPeriod>                      last period in the file |
| <SingleDeclaration>                                one per return, repeated |
| <DeclarationNumber>10000000..99999999</DeclarationNumber> |
| <Employer> |
| <ReferenceNumber>10 digits</ReferenceNumber> |
| <Language>nl \| fr \| de</Language> |
| </Employer> |
| <Revenudeclaration> |
| <Year>EEJJ</Year> |
| <Period>MM00 or a quarter pair</Period> |
| <RevenuNature>2 digits</RevenuNature> |
| <TaxableRevenu>eurocent</TaxableRevenu> |
| <Prepayment>eurocent</Prepayment> |
| <Year325>JJ</Year325>                          facultative |
| </Revenudeclaration> |
| <Receipt> |
| <District>01..13</District> |
| <Office>2 digits</Office> |
| </Receipt> |
| <Payment> |
| <PaymentReference>12 digits</PaymentReference> |
| </Payment> |
| <ThirdDeclarer> |
| <SecretariatCode>4 digits, or 9998</SecretariatCode> |
| <Membership>max 11 characters</Membership> |
| <NewMember/>                                   empty element, facultative |
| </ThirdDeclarer> |
| </SingleDeclaration> |
| </Declaration> |
| <PositiveDeclarations> |
| <Amount>count</Amount> |
| <Total>eurocent, never negative</Total> |
| </PositiveDeclarations> |
| <NegativeDeclarations> |
| <Amount>count</Amount> |
| <Total>eurocent, always negative</Total> |
| </NegativeDeclarations> |
| <OfficeAmount>count</OfficeAmount> |
| </Declaration274> |
|  |
| ═══ MANDATORY SORT ORDER — SingleDeclaration ═══ |
| The SingleDeclaration elements MUST be sorted in ascending order on, in this order: |
|  |
| 1  District |
| 2  Office |
| 3  Language |
| 4  ReferenceNumber |
| 5  Year |
| 6  Period |
| 7  Year325 |
| 8  RevenuNature |
|  |
| Where all eight of these are equal between two SingleDeclaration elements, the |
| declaration is admitted only if at least one of the two remaining elements — |
| TaxableRevenu or Prepayment — differs. |
|  |
| And where several SingleDeclaration elements carry the same eight sort keys, the |
| POSITIVE Prepayment amounts must precede the negative ones. |
|  |
| ═══ CHECK-DIGIT ALGORITHMS — TWO OF THEM, AND THEY ARE NOT THE SAME ═══ |
| Employer/ReferenceNumber (10 digits) |
| digit 1        0 |
| digits 2-8     the first 7 digits of PaymentReference |
| digits 9-10    the COMPLEMENT TO 97 of the remainder of the preceding digits / 97 |
| if the remainder is 00, replace it with 97 |
|  |
| Payment/PaymentReference (12 digits) |
| digits 1-7     the stem of the reference number: |
| the first 7 digits of ReferenceNumber, if that is 9 digits |
| digits 2 to 8 of ReferenceNumber, if that is 10 digits |
| digits 8-10    the period code: numeric, > 600, matching the Year-Period pair |
| digits 11-12   the REMAINDER of the 10 preceding digits / 97 |
| if the remainder is 00, replace it with 97 |
|  |
| Note the difference: the reference number uses the COMPLEMENT to 97, the payment |
| reference uses the REMAINDER itself. Implementing one algorithm for both is the |
| obvious error and it produces a file that is structurally valid and unpayable. |
|  |
| ═══ PERIOD-CODE SERIES — THE ROLLING FOUR-SERIES SCHEME ═══ |
| Digits 8-10 of the PaymentReference carry a period code from one of four series. |
| The series ROTATE: each series is reused every four years, so the mapping from a |
| series to a year changes over time. The file description gives the scheme as at |
| its own date and the rotation rule: |
|  |
| 601 - 634    701 - 734    801 - 834    901 - 934 |
|  |
| from calendar year 2012   900 series refers to 2013 (instead of 2009) |
| from calendar year 2013   600 series refers to 2014 (instead of 2010) |
| from calendar year 2014   800 series refers to 2015 (instead of 2011) |
|  |
| The current-year mapping for income year 2026 is NOT FOUND in the held sources: |
| the file description was written in 2011 and its worked table stops in 2015. The |
| rotation rule is stated, but projecting it forward eleven years to obtain the 2026 |
| series would be a derivation, not a source. It is marked NOT FOUND rather than |
| computed. Requires direct inquiry to info.finprof@minfin.fed.be. |
|  |
| ═══ RESPONSE LEG ═══ |
| IN-07  Finprof acknowledgement — acceptance of the withholding tax return, evidence |
| of filing (CCG Module 10.2). Status is PULLED through the Zoeken function of |
| the FinProf application, not pushed. BE-SIR-001 gap G12 records that no |
| acknowledgement SLA is published. |

### Sheet: `Population Rules`

| Rule Category | Field Name | Source System | Population Logic | Edge Cases |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ═══ MANDATORY FIELD RULES ═══ |  |  |  |  |
| Aggregation | Revenue Nature (RevenuNature) and the SingleDeclaration split | BE-WTC-001 wage types | This return is an aggregate, and the aggregation key is what makes it correct. Produce one SingleDeclaration per distinct combination of District, Office, Language, ReferenceNumber, Year, Period, Year325 and RevenuNature. That means mapping every wage type in BE-WTC-001 that bears withholding onto an income-nature code, then summing the taxable base and the withholding within each code. Ordinary remuneration is nature 10; every exemption regime has its own nature code and therefore its own SingleDeclaration, which is precisely how the return 'reports the exemption separately from the gross withholding' as CCG Module 10.1 requires. | Income nature 08 (overtime) remains in the official list but was ABOLISHED from period April 2007. The engine must reject it at mapping time. A client with more than one collection office, or with employees under more than one language regime, produces more SingleDeclaration elements than a naive one-per-nature implementation will generate. |
| Amount format | TaxableRevenu and Prepayment | Payroll result | Both amounts are expressed in EUROCENT, at most 13 digits, with no decimal separator. A negative amount carries a LEADING minus sign placed before the amount — not a trailing sign and not an overpunched final digit. CCG Module 10.1 lists 'taxable base per employee per month' and 'withholding tax per employee per month' as required payroll intermediates; this return consumes them in aggregate, but the per-employee intermediates must exist because the 281.10 will need them at year end. | Where several SingleDeclaration elements share all eight sort keys, the positive Prepayment amounts must PRECEDE the negative ones. This is an ordering rule inside the file, not merely a sort of the output, and a generator that emits in payroll-run order will breach it. |
| Constants | CoreHeader — MessageType, Origin, DocumentType | Protocol configuration | Three fixed values imposed by the UME2 communication standard: MessageType must contain REQUEST, Origin must contain FINPROF, DocumentType must contain Multiple_PRP_Declaration. They are not configurable and not conditional. | None. If the channel begins rejecting on these, the file description has been superseded — which is exactly the risk BE-SIR-001 gap G13 records, given the source is dated 26 September 2011. |
| ═══ CRITICAL VALIDATION RULES ═══ |  |  |  |  |
| Check digits | Employer/ReferenceNumber | Employer master data | Ten digits: digit 1 is 0; digits 2 to 8 must equal the first seven digits of the PaymentReference element; digits 9 and 10 are the check key, being the COMPLEMENT TO 97 of the remainder of the preceding digits divided by 97, and where that remainder is 00 it is replaced by 97. The number generally corresponds to the enterprise number of the party liable, but the administration exceptionally allocates its own ten-digit reference beginning with 01, so the engine must store the reference as master data rather than deriving it from the enterprise number. | Nine digits instead of ten remains permitted, and the two lengths change how the PaymentReference stem is taken — from the first seven digits for a nine-digit reference, but from digits 2 to 8 for a ten-digit one. An implementation that assumes one length will build a wrong payment reference for the other. |
| Check digits | Payment/PaymentReference | Derived arithmetically | Twelve digits in three parts. Digits 1-7 are the stem of the reference number, taken as described above. Digits 8-10 are the period code, which must be numeric, greater than 600, and equal to the code corresponding to the Year-Period pair. Digits 11-12 are the check digit, being the REMAINDER of the ten preceding digits divided by 97, with 00 replaced by 97. BE-SIR-001 records for OUT-11 that this structured communication is derived arithmetically from the employer reference number and the period code rather than from a mapping table, and that is exactly right — but the period code itself comes from a table. | The two check-digit algorithms in this return are NOT the same: the reference number takes the COMPLEMENT to 97, the payment reference takes the REMAINDER. Implementing one for both yields a file that passes structural validation and produces an unmatched payment. Separately, the period-code series for income year 2026 is NOT FOUND — the source table stops at 2015 — so this field cannot be completed from held sources alone. |
| Ordering | SingleDeclaration sequence | Sender software | The elements must be sorted ascending on District, Office, Language, ReferenceNumber, Year, Period, Year325 and RevenuNature, in that order. Where all eight are equal, the declaration is admitted only if at least one of TaxableRevenu or Prepayment differs between them — so a genuine duplicate is a rejection, not a merge. | Year325 is facultative. Sorting on an optional field requires a defined position for the absent case, and the file description does not state one. Treat absence consistently across the whole file and raise the ambiguity with FPS Finance rather than varying it. |
| Control totals | PositiveDeclarations, NegativeDeclarations, OfficeAmount | Sender software | PositiveDeclarations/Amount counts the Prepayment elements greater than or equal to zero and Total sums them, and that total can NEVER be negative. NegativeDeclarations/Amount counts the Prepayment elements less than zero and Total sums them, and that total must ALWAYS be negative. OfficeAmount counts the collection offices present in the file. Compute all five from the file as actually written, never from the payroll run that produced it. | Note the boundary: a Prepayment of exactly zero counts as POSITIVE, because the positive test is 'greater than or equal to zero'. An implementation that treats zero as neither will produce counts that do not sum to the number of declarations. |
| ═══ PAYROLL-SPECIFIC POPULATION RULES ═══ |  |  |  |  |
| Language | Employer/Language | Employer master data | Set from the region of the employer's SEAT OF OPERATION under CCG Module 1.1 — Dutch in the Dutch-language region, French in the French-language region, German in the German-language region, and in bilingual Brussels the language of the employee. It is not the employee's residence, not the contract language and not a client preference. It is also a sort key of the file, so it partitions the SingleDeclaration elements. | A client with establishments in more than one language region has more than one language value and therefore more than one set of SingleDeclaration elements, even for a single collection office. CCG Module 1.1 also records the sanction for getting the language of a personnel document wrong — nullity in Flanders and Wallonia — which is a different obligation but the same underlying determination. |
| Frequency | Period and the filing cycle | Client configuration | Monthly filers use the MM00 codes; quarterly filers — small employers — use the from-to quarter codes 0103, 0406, 0709 and 1012. Parties liable declaring more than EUR 2,500,000.00 additionally file the 'first 15 days of December' advance under period code 1215, which is a distinct period value and not a variant of 1200. The return and the payment (OUT-11) share the 15th-of-the-following-month deadline. | A client crossing the EUR 2,500,000.00 threshold acquires the December advance obligation mid-year. A client moving between monthly and quarterly filing changes the period-code family, which changes digits 8-10 of the payment reference, which changes the check digit — the whole structured communication is rebuilt, not adjusted. |
| Reconciliation | Annual reconciliation against the payroll ledger | Payroll ledger, BE-FIN-002 | CCG Module 10.5 step 3: reconcile the twelve monthly returns against the payroll ledger in January. Note carefully what this is and is not — it is a reconciliation of what was DECLARED against what was PAID, not a recomputation of any employee's tax. Module 10.5 states there is NO annual tax reconciliation in Belgian payroll. The reconciliation matters because the 281.10 (BE-FIN-002) is built independently from the payroll ledger and must agree with these returns; a divergence means one of the two is wrong. | A divergence found in January for the prior income year may fall outside the withholding-tax correction windows. For income year 2025 those closed on 15 May 2026 for exemption-related corrections and 10 July 2026 for others, and the channel closed entirely on 31 August 2026 (CCG Module 10.5). Reconcile early enough to correct. |
| ═══ CROSS-FIELD VALIDATIONS ═══ |  |  |  |  |
| Cross-field | ReferenceNumber digits 2-8 vs PaymentReference digits 1-7 | Both | These two must agree by construction. The file description states the relationship from both directions — the reference number's digits 2 to 8 must correspond to the first seven digits of the PaymentReference, and the PaymentReference's first seven digits are the stem of the reference number. Build one from the other rather than sourcing them independently, and validate the agreement before sending. | The stem is taken differently depending on whether the reference number is nine or ten digits. A client whose reference number length changes — which happens when the administration allocates its own 01-prefixed number — invalidates every stored payment reference for that client. |
| Cross-field | PaymentReference digits 8-10 vs Year and Period | Both | The period code embedded in the payment reference must equal the code corresponding to the Year-Period pair declared in the Revenudeclaration. The two travel together: the return says which period is being declared and the payment reference says which period is being paid, and a mismatch produces a payment that cannot be allocated. | This is the field the income-year-2026 series gap bites on. The rotation rule is published and the four series are published, but the source's worked mapping stops at 2015 and has NOT been projected forward in this specification. Until FPS Finance confirms the current series, this cross-validation cannot be implemented. |
| Cross-filing | This return vs the DmfA vs the 281.10 | BE-NSSO-002, BE-FIN-002 | Three filings drawing on overlapping payroll data, none derived from another. CCG Module 10.1: the withholding tax return is separate from the DmfA, with a different authority on a different cycle; and the Belcotax annual filing is NOT generated from the twelve monthly returns but is an independent filing that must be reconciled against them. Build all three from the payroll ledger and reconcile, rather than deriving any one from another. | The correction cascade of CCG Module 10.5 runs the other way: a corrective DmfA changes the net, which changes the taxable base, which changes both this return and the 281.10. Because the three have different deadlines, a single underlying error can be correctable in one filing and time-barred in another. |

### Sheet: `Payroll Scope Summary`

| Belcotax-on-web 281.10 — PAYROLL SCOPE SUMMARY |  |  |
| --- | --- | --- |
|  |  |  |
| What goes on the annual certificate, and — as importantly — where it comes from. CCG Module 10.1: this is an INDEPENDENT filing built from the payroll ledger. It is not generated from the DmfA and it is not generated from the twelve monthly withholding tax returns; it must be reconciled against them. |  |  |
|  |  |  |
| ITEM / SCENARIO | IN SCOPE? | NOTES / REASONING |
| ═══ WHO GETS A FICHE ═══ |  |  |
| Every employee who received remuneration in the income year | YES | One fiche per recipient, keyed on the sequence number in zone 2.009 and identified by the national number in zone 2.011. |
| An employee who left during the income year | YES | Zone 2.056 carries the date of departure, and the departure holiday pay goes to box 251 and the termination indemnity to box 308. |
| An employee who joined during the income year | YES | Zone 2.055 carries the date of entry into service. |
| Non-residents | YES | Zone 2.018 carries a non-zero country of residence, which switches the postal code from zone 2.016 to zone 2.112. The brochure requires the national or BIS number for non-residents specifically. |
| Students under a student contract | YES | Zone 2.136 repeats the total student remuneration for information — it is ALREADY included in the other boxes and is not an additional amount. |
| Flexi-job workers | YES | Box 262 for a non-pensioner (zone 2.198); zone 2.166 for a pensioner, which follows a different treatment. |
| Data that belong only in the 325.10 summary | PARTIAL | Zone 2.029 value 1: the data are NOT the subject of a fiche 281.10 and serve only for inclusion in the 325.10 statement. The brochure notes this may also be used for harvest wages where the withholding is discharging. |
| Public sector personnel without an employment contract | NO | Zone 2.041 and box 290, and the December remuneration box 247. Out of scope for this build, consistent with BE-NSSO-002. |
| Sportspersons, referees, trainers | NO | Boxes 273 to 280. Sector-specific; BE-WTC-001 carries no sports-sector wage types, so this build cannot populate them. |
| ═══ TIMING AND RELATIONSHIP ═══ |  |  |
| Generated from the twelve monthly withholding tax returns | NO | CCG Module 10.1 states this explicitly and control C4 repeats it: it is an independent filing built from the payroll ledger. Deriving it from the 274 returns is wrong in principle even where it balances. |
| Generated from the DmfA | NO | A different authority, a different base and a different period basis. The DmfA is quarterly and social security; this is annual and tax. |
| Reconciled against the monthly returns | YES | CCG Module 10.5 step 3. A divergence means one of the two is wrong, and it must be found before the correction windows close. |
| Issued to the employee | YES | CCG Module 10.5 step 5: produce and issue form 281.10 to each employee before the Belcotax deadline. |
| The 325.10 filed separately | NO | BE-SIR-001 2.1: derived by FPS Finance from the 281.10 data, not separately submitted. |
| ═══ AMOUNTS AND CALCULATIONS ═══ |  |  |
| Amounts carried in the 13-digit numeric zones | YES | Zones in the ranges 2.059-2.088, 2.110-2.143 and 2.176-2.245 are 13 N. The brochure's zone-range table gives MAXIMUM lengths across all fiche types; the exact maximum for 281.10 is in the XSD, which is not held. |
| Overtime hours in HUNDREDTHS of an hour | YES | The brochure carries the warning explicitly and repeatedly: 'Opgelet: overuren in honderdsten van uren'. It applies to zones 2.095, 2.097, 2.110, 2.118, 2.142, 2.167-2.170, 2.176, 2.196, 2.199, 2.209 and 2.228. |
| Share option percentages in a fixed five-character format | YES | dd,dd — exactly five characters, the leading zero AND the comma always transmitted, multiple percentages separated by a colon. Exchange-listed or traded options carry '00,00'. |
| Control total computed by the sender | YES | Zone 2.059: the total of zones 2.060 to 2.088 inclusive. It is a checksum, not a payroll figure. |
| Employee tax recomputed | NO | CCG Module 10.5: there is no annual tax reconciliation in Belgian payroll. The employee settles through the personal income tax return. |
| ═══ SPECIAL CASES ═══ |  |  |
| Correction after filing | YES | Zone 2.028 is the mechanism: 0 = ordinary, 1 = modification, 2 = addition, 3 = annulment. CCG Module 10.5: a corrective filing through Belcotax-on-web produces a corrected certificate for the employee, and it is made as soon as identified. |
| Horeca overtime split by whether a registered cash register is in use | YES | Boxes 335-338 without, boxes 395-398 with. CCG Module 4.4: the registered cash register raises the overtime relief ceiling. BE-SIR-001 2.4 registers the cash register itself as out of scope but records that a per-employer flag is the data contract it implies — this is where that flag lands. |
| Construction overtime with electronic attendance registration | YES | Zone 2.176, feeding box 305. The attendance registration itself is OUT-18, which is out of scope, but its output changes this box. |
| Benefits in kind with multiple natures | YES | Zone 2.099 takes several letter codes placed NEXT TO EACH OTHER with no separator, left-aligned — for example ABC. |

### Sheet: `File Structure`

| Belcotax-on-web 281.10 — FILE STRUCTURE AND TECHNICAL SPECIFICATIONS |
| --- |
|  |
| ═══ FILE FORMAT ═══ |
| Format            XML. |
| Schema            belcotax-2025.xsd (named per income year). |
| Conversion        The validation module converts the validated XML into the encoded |
| .bow format before sending. The .bow file is what is transmitted. |
| Encoding          NOT FOUND - requires direct inquiry (BE-SIR-001 gap G14). The brochure |
| prescribes amounts, dates and structure but not encoding. Resolvable |
| from belcotax-2025.xsd; otherwise belcotax@minfin.fed.be. |
| Size limit        NOT FOUND - not published (gap G14). |
| Alternative       Online entry through 'Verzending per codering'. |
|  |
| ═══ RECORD HIERARCHY ═══ |
| Consignment start record        tags v0…    identifies the sender and the consignment |
| Belcotax declaration record   tags a1…    identifies the debtor of the income |
| Data record — generic part  tags f2…    zones 2001-2029 plus 2105, 2012, 2114 |
| Data record — fiche part    tags f10…   the 119 tags specific to fiche 281.10 |
|  |
| The brochure splits the generic data record into three parts: |
| zones 2001-2009            uniquely define the record |
| zones 2010-2029            plus 2105, 2012 and 2114 — data present on EVERY 281.xx fiche |
| the remaining zones        content determined by the fiche identifier in zone 2008 |
|  |
| ═══ LENGTH AND TYPE BY ZONE RANGE — BROCHURE SECTION 4.2.3.1 ═══ |
| These are MAXIMUM lengths across ALL fiche types. The brochure's own footnote states |
| that for a specific fiche type the length may be shorter, and that the exact maximum |
| is given in the XSD describing the XML to be sent to Belcotax. The XSD is NOT held in |
| 00-official-sources, so the per-fiche maxima cannot be stated here. |
|  |
| 2030-2044    1 N          2113          13 N |
| 2045         3 AN         2115-2117     13 N |
| 2046-2049    3 N          2118          4 N |
| 2050-2054    2 N          2119-2138     13 N |
| 2055-2056    10 DATE      2139-2140     AN |
| 2057-2058    4 N          2141          13 N |
| 2059-2088    13 N         2142          4 N |
| 2089-2092    2 N          2143          13 N |
| 2093         10 DATE      2144          10 DATE |
| 2094         2 N          2150-2152     XML |
| 2095         13 N         2153-2156     AN |
| 2096         2 N          2157-2158     10 DATE |
| 2097         13 N         2159-2160     XML |
| 2098         2 N          2161-2164     10 DATE |
| 2099-2100    AN           2165-2166     13 N |
| 2101         3 N          2167-2170     4 N |
| 2102-2103    AN           2171-2175     10 DATE |
| 2104         2 N          2176-2210     13 N |
| 2106-2107    AN           2211-2215     XML |
| 2108         2 N          2216-2220     DATE |
| 2109         AN           2221-2225     AN |
| 2110-2111    13 N         2226-2245     13 N |
|  |
| ═══ TWO STRICT FORMAT RULES THE BROCHURE SINGLES OUT ═══ |
| SHARE OPTION PERCENTAGES — zone 2.106 (and the same zone on fiche 281.20) |
| Format:   dd,dd    or   dd,dd:dd,dd:dd,dd …    or empty |
| where d is a digit 0-9. |
| The percentage must be given with two digits, then two digits after the decimal |
| separator. Where there are several, they are separated by a COLON. |
| A percentage must ALWAYS consist of 5 characters, and the leading 0 and the comma |
| must ALWAYS be transmitted. |
| Exchange-listed or traded options: enter '00,00'. |
|  |
| OVERTIME IN HUNDREDTHS OF AN HOUR |
| The brochure repeats the warning at every overtime zone: 'Opgelet: overuren in |
| honderdsten van uren'. 7 hours 40 minutes is 766, not 740 and not 7.40. |
